evidence_items.summary: Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as conversational agents for communication and guidance, but their ability to adapt responses to a patient’s emotional state and literacy level remains insufficiently characterized. In patient-facing scenarios, effective communication requires not only accurate medical content but also appropriate tone, clarity, and responsiveness to user vulnerability. Objective This study aimed to evaluate, within a controlled, single-scenario experimental design, the ability of contemporary LLMs to adapt medical guidance responses to different levels of emotional sensitivity and literacy, and to assess their consistency in both generating and interpreting such adaptations. Methods A controlled benchmark was designed to evaluate how 4 LLMs adapt medical guidance responses to predefined emotional and literacy levels for a realistic patient profile asking an open-ended question. To establish a robust performance baseline, one model was deployed locally (Gemma 3 27B), and 3 are cloud-based (Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro, and GPT 5.2). Each model was tested across all combinations of 5 emotional levels, 3 literacy levels, and 3 prompt-verbosity variants, yielding 45 responses per model. Generated responses were assessed against human-reviewed ground truth for emotional and literacy alignment. A separate self-evaluation procedure measured each model’s ability to interpret its own outputs using the same adaptation framework. The study also examined generation-interpretation consistency and quantitative text properties, with particular attention to response length and verbosity. Results Literacy adaptation was consistently accurate across models, often achieving near-zero error, indicating strong capability in adjusting explanatory complexity. In contrast, emotional adaptation showed greater variability and was more sensitive to model architecture and prompt design.
evidence_items.title: Emotional and Literacy Adaptation in Large Language Model–Based Medical Guidance: Development and Usability Study

evidence_items.summary: Product design is a complex, knowledge-based process that balances customer needs with engineering constraints and market realities. While traditional methods such as Quality Function Deployment (QFD) and machine learning (ML) have improved the design process and solutions, they still struggle with flexibility and a deep semantic understanding of design requirements. Advances in Large Language Models (LLMs), powered by Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), create new opportunities for intelligent, human-centred support for product design. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this systematic review analyzes 1,263 studies published between 2023 and 2026 to answer three questions: (1) how LLMs are applied across design stages, (2) how these systems are evaluated, and (3) what gaps remain. We found that LLMs successfully support design requirements analysis, ideation, and documentation. However, current evaluation methods lack standardized benchmarks for design quality. Persistent challenges remain, including hallucinations, weak domain grounding, tool-integration hurdles, and ethical concerns. To guide future research, we introduce a technical maturity map that highlights current achievements and uninvestigated areas in design systems and suggests a roadmap for applying LLMs in product design.
evidence_items.title: Large Language Models in Product Design: A Review

organizations: Department of Pulmonology, Affiliated Hospital of Changchun University of Chinese Medicine
The Affiliated Hospital to Changchun University of Chinese Medicine
evidence_items.summary: Differentiating Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) respiratory syndromes requires weighing overlapping symptoms together with tongue and pulse findings, a task that most AI systems for TCM perform end-to-end but without an interpretable intermediate representation. In this study, we addressed this gap with LEAF (LLM extraction and multiobjective feature selection), a two-stage modular framework evaluated on 3,253 records covering 14 respiratory syndromes from the TCM-SD benchmark. Its first large language model (LLM) stage extracted a 35-item symptom ontology that was built entirely from public TCM sources; among three interchangeable LLMs, Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct was ranked as the best, followed by Phi-4 and the TCM domain model BianCang. Its second evolutionary-computation stage benchmarked four multiobjective evolutionary algorithms [non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm-II (NSGA-II), strength Pareto evolutionary algorithm 2 (SPEA2), competitive mechanism-based multiobjective particle swarm optimizer (CMOPSO), and non-dominated sorting differential evolution (NSDE)] over 10 seeds, and they were compared using Friedman’s and Nemenyi’s testing in terms of both classification outcome and search-process quality. The four algorithms showed no significant separation on held-out macro-F1, although NSDE led nominally, and none exceeded the full-feature baseline on point estimates. In contrast, hypervolume differed significantly and favored NSGA-II, the weakest of the four on held-out macro-F1. A four-classifier panel found no algorithm to be significantly different from either the full-feature baseline or a random-feature control, which was significantly outperformed only by the full-feature baseline. Applying NSDE to the remaining two LLM pipelines reproduced the original ranking, and its representative solution was fully attested against the knowledge base of TCM-SD, although not typically so across all the 10 seeds.
evidence_items.title: LEAF: benchmarking multiobjective evolutionary feature selection over large language model–extracted symptoms for interpretable Traditional Chinese Medicine respiratory syndrome differentiation

organizations: 1School of Earth Sciences, University of Bristol, Bristol, United Kingdom
2Department of Earth Sciences, University of Oxford, Oxford, United Kingdom
evidence_items.summary: ABSTRACT Microseismic monitoring is often used at subsurface industrial sites, such as hydraulic fracturing for shale gas, stimulation of engineered geothermal systems, mature hydrocarbon reservoirs, and carbon capture and storage. Microseismic observations can be used to map growing fractures in the subsurface, to understand the geomechanical response of subsurface reservoirs to industrial operations, and to identify and characterize nascent induced seismicity. Downhole microseismic datasets are acquired using multistation geophone strings placed in deep boreholes at reservoir depths, with sampling rates at 1 kHz or higher. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools have driven a step-change in the processing of surface-based seismological data. However, similar improvements are yet to be realized for downhole microseismic processing tasks. To date, a major barrier in the development of AI tools for downhole microseismic monitoring has been the lack of publicly available data with which to train models. We seek to eliminate this barrier by curating an AI-ready downhole microseismic benchmark database (AMBER) consisting of waveforms and labels (arrival time picks) drawn from 10 downhole microseismic datasets. AMBER contains over 4,000 events with over 150,000 individual P and S wave picks. All picks have been manually verified. The database also contains over 10,000 examples of signal-free noise, which have also been manually verified. The database is provided in an AI-ready format, with Python functions for data ingestion and data augmentation. It is hoped that AMBER will stimulate and support the development of AI tools for downhole microseismic processing.
evidence_items.title: The AI-Ready Downhole Microseismic Benchmark Database (AMBER)

evidence_items.summary: Direct beamforming methods in photoacoustic computed tomography are often compared under idealized conditions, making it difficult to distinguish artifact suppression from the preservation of weak structures. We benchmark seven direct beamforming methods and four limited-view adaptive minimum-variance variants in heterogeneous two-dimensional photoacoustic computed tomography simulations that incorporate fluence variation, full-wave acoustic propagation, finite-aperture detection, measurement noise, and incomplete angular coverage. Eleven phantoms were evaluated over multiple signal-to-noise ratios using phantom-level statistics. The delay-and-sum method most consistently preserved extended low-amplitude structures, achieved the highest peak signal-to-noise ratio among the direct methods, and showed the lowest mean globally scaled amplitude error. Coherence-, variance-, and multiplication-based weighting reduced clutter and often narrowed point responses, but also increasingly attenuated weak targets. Under severe full-view noise, delay-multiply-and-sum and delay-and-sum-to-delay-standard-deviation-factor weighting improved structural similarity while reducing peak signal-to-noise ratio and the Dice coefficient. In limited-view imaging, spatially smoothed minimum-variance beamforming produced small gains in structural similarity at 0 and −5 dB but lower peak signal-to-noise ratio, Dice coefficient, and generalized contrast-to-noise ratio. Sound-speed perturbations did not alter the leading ranking of the direct methods, while spatial point-target analysis revealed strong anisotropy. Cleaner or narrower reconstructions did not necessarily provide better preservation of structure or amplitude.
evidence_items.title: Direct beamforming for heterogeneous photoacoustic computed tomography: a two-dimensional benchmark

organizations: Department of Chemistry, National Dong Hwa University, Hualien 974301, Taiwan
evidence_items.summary: Virtual screening answers two different questions with one number: enrichment, separating actives from background molecules, and potency ranking, ordering actives by measured activity. We benchmarked both for the same score on the same compounds across five CNS binding sites (SERT, GABAA benzodiazepine site, 5-HT1A, σ1, and NMDA MK-801 pore), docking ChEMBL actives, inactives, and property-matched decoys with Uni-Dock and GNINA under a held-out normalisation/evaluation split, plus an experimentally characterised negative probe excluded from all fitting. Ranking, evaluated among pChEMBL ≥ 7 actives, was negligible for every target (median Spearman ρ = 0.020) and was not recovered by data-quality filtering, multivariate null models, scaffold-aware resampling, strict assay–site matching with rebuilt decoys, or stricter curation. Enrichment proved strongly benchmark-dependent: an apparent ΔAUC gain of +0.153 against molecular weight-matched decoys decreased to ≤0.05 once the decoys were matched to seven descriptors, and the residue was not robust to compound resampling. A classifier using no structural information separated the same actives from the same decoys at ROC-AUC 0.959–0.993, and cognate ligand redocking reproduced the crystallographic pose as the top-ranked solution for one of five targets. Benchmark enrichment should not be equated with protein-specific recognition; the benchmark, the poses, and the ranking require separate validation.
evidence_items.title: A Decision-Centric Benchmark of Enrichment and Potency Ranking in CNN-Rescored Molecular Docking

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Dependable comparisons of minimum weighted feedback arc set (MWFAS) heuristics require consistent inputs, computational budgets, and treatment of incomplete runs. We present an audited benchmark linking weighted graphs and source-parent relationships to validated saved orders, original outcomes, and numerical optimization references. This resource extends an earlier metrics-only release and supports comparisons across graph families, paired weight regimes, and empirical sources. Incumbent-protected strongly connected component neighborhood search (IPSNS) showed family-dependent gains over its better initializer. Across all tested graph--seed groups in two generated-graph campaigns, ten iterations produced the same saved objectives and permutations as every larger tested budget. In the replicated campaign, family median process-wall ratios relative to the selected initializer were 1.27--1.60 at ten iterations, compared with 3.19--9.82 at 200. This observed trade-off is not a convergence or stopping guarantee. Under matched wall-clock horizons, IPSNS seed~1 beat RASstar on seven of nine selected synthetic topologies but only one of four selected empirical parents. At 300~s, single-node insertion from either evaluated initializer beat IPSNS seed~1 on all four parents. In a separate empirical campaign, complete 200-iteration comparisons covered only 18 of 38 views, all from one source parent. These findings show how budget, availability, dependence, and comparator choice affect interpretation. Public saved-output replay covers all ten numerical tables, Figure~2, and 11/17 tracked claim groups; six broader groups and historical-source reconstruction remain unresolved. The evidence supports scoped comparisons of existing methods rather than a universal ranking.
evidence_items.title: An Audited Benchmark for Minimum Weighted Feedback Arc Set: Graph Identity, Algorithm Comparison, and Reproducibility

organizations: Faculty of Computers and Articial Intelligence, Sohag University, Egypt
International Graduate School of Articial Intelligence, National Yunlin University of Science and Technology, Douliu 64002, Taiwan, R.O.C.
evidence_items.summary: Multi-criteria decision systems often interpret disagreement among criteria as evidence that some criteria are unreliable. This is problematic when the disagreement reflects a genuine operational trade-off. We develop a reliability-and-admissibility-calibrated q-rung orthopair neutrosophic soft ranking procedure (RAC-qRON) that distinguishes recorded evidence quality from the direction of criterion preferences. An explicitly bounded interval for each alternative–criterion observation is mapped to truth, indeterminacy and falsity memberships, with an admissibility proof for every integer rung q ≥ 1. Criterion weights are adjusted according to recorded information coverage rather than cross-criterion correlation, and a fixed-reference ideal-distance calculation produces an auditable rank. The method is evaluated on 21 historical operating records from an ammonia-oxidation plant, using the published Brownlee stack-loss data, four transparently specified criteria and no fictitious expert panel. With q = 3, the leading historical observation is day 21 (closeness 0.6885). Under 10% randomly masked cells, the mean Kendall rank correlation with the respective complete-data ranking is 0.750 for RAC-qRON, versus 0.806 for median-imputed TOPSIS; the model therefore does not exhibit superior missing-data stability. Rung sensitivity also changes the winning observation. The principal contribution is a mathematically admissible, evidence-traceable decision layer and a reproducible diagnosis of its strengths and limitations, rather than an unsupported claim of universal ranking superiority.
evidence_items.title: Reliability-Calibrated Q-Rung Orthopair Neutrosophic Soft Ranking Under Partial Observability: An Auditable Industrial-Process Benchmark

organizations: School of Electrical & Computer Engineering, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Beer-Sheva 8410501, Israel
Department of Physics, Presidency University, Bengaluru 560064, India
Ilse Katz Institute for Nanoscale Science and Technology, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Beer-Sheva 8410501, Israel
evidence_items.summary: Organic and polymer semiconductors are central to modern electronic and optoelectronic technologies, including organic thin-film transistors (OTFTs), solar cells, and bioelectronic devices. Controlling thin-film morphology is critical for optimizing the performance of organic electronic devices. However, the spin-coating process provides limited morphological control, and conventional characterization tools such as X-ray diffraction (XRD) and atomic force microscopy (AFM) are often insensitive to subtle structural changes that strongly influence charge transport. In this work, we demonstrate that spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) combined with critical point (CP) analysis enables rapid, non-destructive assessment of microstructural evolution in regioregular poly(3-hexylthiophene) (rr-P3HT) thin films during thermal annealing. OTFTs based on P3HT were selected as a benchmark system due to their simple device architecture and well-defined structure–property relationships. The CP model provides physically meaningful optical parameters (transition energy, amplitude, broadening, and dimensionality) that correlate with electrical performance. Our results reveal a distinct shift in dimensionality of the primary optical transition upon annealing, indicating increased molecular ordering and reduced energetic disorder. These optically derived descriptors complement conventional structural probes and correlate with the observed improvements in charge transport. These findings offer a practical, non-destructive materials-focused approach for early-stage evaluation and process monitoring in organic electronics.
evidence_items.title: From Optical Transitions Through Morphology Changes to Charge Transport: A P3HT Benchmark Study Using the Critical Point Model

organizations: School of Computer and Mathematical Sciences, University of Nottingham Malaysia
Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Clinical Sciences, Faculty of Dentistry, Universiti Malaya
Oral Cancer Research and Coordinating Centre, Faculty of Dentistry, Universiti Malaya
evidence_items.summary: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) for oral screening is usually judged by aggregate detection metrics on public benchmarks whose partitions, labels, and relevance to users are rarely checked. Methods We audited a prototype combining a YOLOv8m detector for six conditions (1,500 test images), a DenseNet169 histopathology network, and a ResNet18 router. Under a pre-specified plan, we measured duplication across partitions, tested removal of duplicated test images against 10,000 matched controls, compared duplicated copies' labels and predictions, compared the library versions, and ran every test image through the application pipeline. Results Near-duplicates of training images accounted for 17.3% of test and 17.1% of validation images (lower bounds). Removing duplicated test images changed mean average precision (mAP)@0.5 by +0.001 (95% confidence interval [CI] −0.012 to +0.014). Only 22% of duplicated photographs had identical labels on both copies; exploratory analysis suggested memorization of training labels in orientations seen in training. A library update moved mAP@0.5:0.95 by −0.012 with identical predictions. The router rejected 23% of in-domain photographs and 51% of photographs with ulcers, so ulcer sensitivity per image was 0.36 despite the highest benchmark recall (0.91). A class-mapping defect, still live in a public demonstration in September 2026, gave the wrong name to 73% of findings. The histopathology classifier classified every image as positive; its label was not a diagnosis. Conclusion Duplication compromised the benchmark's independence without detectably changing aggregate mAP; the defects that changed what was reported or displayed lay in the labels, evaluation software, and pipeline. Evaluations should verify partitions and labels, pin the library, and test deployed systems end to end.
evidence_items.title: From benchmark to user: an end-to-end evaluation audit of an AI-based oral health screening prototype

organizations: Facultad de Informática, Universidad Autónoma de Querétaro, Av. de las Ciencias s/n, Campus Juriquilla, Querétaro 76230, Mexico
Facultad de Ingeniería, Universidad Autónoma de Querétaro, Querétaro 76010, Mexico

evidence_items.summary: Deep learning solar forecasters depend strongly on their hyperparameters, yet comparisons of hyperparameter optimization methods usually rely on few runs per optimizer, confounding the optimizer with the random seed. A protocol is proposed that tests whether optimizers are practically equivalent and how reliable published comparison designs are. Seven methods (four metaheuristics, two model-based methods, one of them multi-fidelity, and Random Search) tuned three deep networks for one-hour-ahead forecasting of global horizontal irradiance in Querétaro, Mexico, with public reanalysis data, a shared search space, one hundred evaluations, and thirty paired seeds, in nine hundred and thirty runs across all experiments. The tuned models improved on smart persistence by 4–11% in mean absolute error. With the 10-epoch search objective, no pair of optimizers differed after Holm correction, 62 of 63 pairs were equivalent within 1 W/m2, and the optimizer explained 0.8% of the error variance, compared with 7.9% for the seed. In a higher-fidelity check with 50 epochs, two guided methods improved on Random Search by 0.74 W/m2, significantly for one of them, while remaining equivalent to each other, suggesting that, in this setting, objective fidelity mattered more than the choice among guided optimizers. In emulations of published designs, even with 30 runs, 2 studies agreed on the winner in at most 55% of cases. A validated surrogate benchmark, code, data, and predictions are released.
evidence_items.title: Comparative Benchmark of Metaheuristic and Model-Based Hyperparameter Optimization for Deep Learning Models in Global Solar Irradiance Forecasting

organizations: Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research (Birmensdorf, Switzerland)
evidence_items.summary: Abstract. Available water capacity (AWC) is a fundamental soil hydraulic property controlling plant water supply and drought response, yet existing AWC estimates for Switzerland's forests are an order of magnitude coarser than the scale of an individual tree’s root system. Here we produce 25 m resolution maps of mineral soil AWC for Switzerland's forest soils using ten published pedotransfer functions (PTFs) applied to a common set of gridded 25 m digital soil maps. We introduce a novel method for evaluating these PTF-derived AWC estimates using early leaf discoloration, an indicator of extreme drought stress, in European beech (Fagus sylvatica L.). Performance of single feature logistic regression models, using estimated AWC as a predictive feature and September 2018 early leaf discoloration as a target, varied substantially by PTF (ROC-AUC between 0.42 and 0.63). The strongest relationships between AWC and discoloration showed a negative trend and relatively strong model calibration (R² up to 0.82). Combining AWC with total 2018 summer precipitation and maximum 2018 summer temperature had little impact on model discrimination, but improved model calibration (R² up to 0.90) in late summer 2018 with discoloration proportions of nearly 80% at the most susceptible sites. Averaging the results of the four comparatively best-performing PTFs in these models produced two 25 m soil AWC products for the Swiss forest (mean 1 m and 2 m depth AWC) with uncertainty estimates based on variation among PTFs (± 1σ). While both the mapped AWC values and the relative performance of individual PTFs remain dependent on soil properties of the underlying digital soil maps, these new AWC estimates are immediately applicable to forest drought monitoring and species distribution, ecohydrological, and land-surface modelling.
evidence_items.title: Extreme drought stress provides an ecological benchmark for high-resolution available water capacity maps of Swiss forest soils

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Materials literature contains detailed experimental knowledge, but procedures, chemical entities and measurements remain difficult to aggregate because they are reported in heterogeneous forms and depend on process-specific context. We present SciKGExtract, a schema-guided framework that combines large-language-model extraction with chemical normalization and agent-based evaluation and refinement before knowledge-graph integration. We evaluate the framework on 176 atomic-layer-deposition papers describing zinc oxide (ZnO) and indium--gallium--zinc oxide (IGZO), together with an expert-annotated full-schema subset. PubChem normalization improves exact-match extraction F1 for every tested model. For ZnO, the best F1 increases from 0.591 for direct normalized extraction to 0.805 with agentic refinement, whereas the best IGZO result is 0.344, revealing the greater difficulty of multicomponent supercycle processes. Evaluation against a deeply nested schema containing 65 experimental properties and 155 quantitative measurement nodes further exposes errors in process segmentation and numerical assignment. These results show that chemical canonicalization and targeted agentic verification provide complementary controls for converting complex materials literature into reusable, machine-actionable experimental knowledge.
evidence_items.title: Agentic schema-guided extraction of materials process knowledge from scientific literature

evidence_items.summary: Enterprise agentic AI systems exchange contextual information across functional modules, creating governance challenges when information crosses operational and organizational boundaries. This study distinguishes organizational governance boundaries from information exchange boundaries and proposes an Inter-Module Information Contract (IMIC) architecture for purpose-bounded context exchange. IMIC evaluates provenance, semantic and temporal validity, permitted information scope, and applicable originating constraints before downstream execution, independently of language-model reasoning. We compare IMIC with full-context sharing, reduced-context sharing, and strengthened structured handoff. In a deterministic benchmark of 32 synthetic conditions, joint correctness is achieved in 3, 10, 28, and 32 cases, respectively. The four differences between strengthened structured handoff and IMIC arise from conditions testing onward-transfer permission, recipient, purpose, and field scope. A downstream integration experiment evaluates 14 selected conditions across four local language models and three seeds, yielding 168 case–model–seed blocks and 672 method-level records. IMIC achieves correct exchange actions and information boundaries in all 168 blocks and joint correctness in 165 across four local LLMs and three seeds. Three permitted executions produce incorrect downstream responses despite correctly governed exchanges, demonstrating that information-exchange correctness does not guarantee correct downstream task performance. These results support the functional feasibility of the implemented originating-contract inheritance mechanism under controlled synthetic conditions. Generalizability to independent enterprise workflows, richer policy structures, multiple information providers, and derived information requires further validation.
evidence_items.title: Purpose-Bounded Context Exchange in Enterprise Agentic AI Systems: An Inter-Module Information Contract Architecture

evidence_items.summary: Background Physicians increasingly use artificial intelligence tools to support clinical work, yet there is no accepted standard for measuring the competency of large language models (LLMs) in clinical decision support. We developed EM-BENCH, a physician-validated, deterministically scored benchmark for evaluating whether models reliably apply the American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP) guidelines to clinical decisions. Methods EM-BENCH comprises 210 binary clinical vignettes covering all 70 critical questions across 25 ACEP clinical policies. We evaluated 149 LLM configurations representing 79 base models using prespecified answers and deterministic scoring. Each vignette had a prespecified correct answer to a binary yes-or-no question based on an ACEP recommendation. We examined associations between accuracy and model access tier (closed-access vs. open-weight models), model size, release date, clinical policy, recommendation evidence level, and reasoning settings. Results No configuration achieved complete guideline concordance. The highest performing configuration answered 207 of 210 vignettes correctly (98.6%). Closed-access models outperformed open-weight models (median accuracy, 91% vs. 63%; Hodges-Lehmann location shift, 26 percentage points; 99% CI, 20 to 33; adjusted P<0.001). Among open-weight model families, a 10-fold increase in parameter count was associated with a 14-percentage-point increase in accuracy (99% CI, 7.7 to 20; adjusted P<0.001). Across all models, accuracy increased by 8.9 percentage points per release year (99% CI, 3.6 to 14; adjusted P<0.001). Neither enabling a thinking mode (pseudomedian change, 0.95 percentage points; 99% CI, -2.6 to 3.1; adjusted P=1.00) nor high versus low reasoning effort (0.91 percentage points; 99% CI, -0.69 to 3.1; adjusted P=0.56) consistently improved accuracy. Conclusions Contemporary LLMs showed improving but incomplete ability to apply ACEP guidelines. Concordance varied markedly across models and was associated with access tier, size, and release recency, while additional inference-time reasoning offered inconsistent benefit. Specialty-specific, physician-validated benchmarks may provide a reproducible assessment of LLMs' ability to make guideline-concordant clinical decisions.
evidence_items.title: EM-BENCH: A Reproducible Framework for Benchmarking Guideline-Concordant Clinical Decision Making in Large Language Models

evidence_items.summary: Fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles experience operating-condition transitions, asynchronous sensor sampling, and control-system compensation that can obscure fault signatures. Existing temporal detection methods have limited capacity to represent coupled faults across subsystems, track their evolution, and constrain language-model diagnoses with quantitative evidence. This paper proposes TGTV, an interpretable fault detection and traceability framework that integrates spatiotemporal graph learning with a large language model. A temporal convolutional network and a graph attention network with weighted fused adjacency extract multiscale temporal patterns and spatial dependencies among sensors. A hybrid temporal Transformer and variational autoencoder then evaluates window-level anomalies using prediction errors and reconstruction probabilities. Continuous-time Shapley attribution identifies critical sensors and high-contribution intervals while preserving the temporal continuity of fault evolution. A structured evidence package combines detection results, graph relationships, temporal attribution, sensor attribution, and operating context. An evidence-constrained diagnosis protocol uses this package to generate flight-level conclusions with traceable evidence identifiers. Cross-flight holdout experiments on the public ALFA fixed-wing flight dataset yield a window-level area under the precision-recall curve of 0.976, accuracy of 0.973, recall of 0.902, and F1 score of 0.920. Flight-level fault diagnosis achieves recall of 0.943 and an F1 score of 0.944. These results demonstrate accurate anomaly detection and quantitatively supported fault-tracing cues, providing a basis for interpretable post-flight fault review and analysis.
evidence_items.title: TGTV: An Interpretable Framework for UAV Fault Detection and Traceability via Spatiotemporal Graph Learning and Large Language Models

evidence_items.summary: Two-dimensional (2D) materials exhibit distinctive physical, chemical, and electronic-structure properties that make them highly attractive for energy storage and conversion applications. However, the synthesis routes, performance metrics, and article-level metadata are scattered across different literature studies, which are difficult to standardize and reuse systematically. To this end, we have developed an end-to-end framework for literature knowledge extraction, data management and data mining. Based on large language models (LLMs), the framework is enhanced by domain-informed context engineering and lightweight fine-tuning. It has successfully extracted the structured information from approximately 50 000 research papers and integrated the extracted data into a relational knowledge base that contains 600 200 performance records and 202 300 synthesis records. The constructed knowledge database is supported by our proposed multi-agent SQL workflow for natural-language retrieval. To further assess the utility of the extracted knowledge, we have incorporated the band-gap records in the literature into the C2DB-based band-gap prediction benchmark to conduct the external evaluation by using five-fold cross-validation. The inclusion of the extracted records yielded stable mean R2 and pooled MAE. Further SHAP analysis indicates that the model predictions are mainly driven by physically meaningful descriptors related to thermodynamic stability, elemental periodicity, local coordination environments, and learned CHGNet representations. The results show that the LLM-extracted literature data are not only the searchable text resources, but also can be incorporated into quantitative modeling and interpretability analysis, thereby facilitating data-driven materials discovery, performance optimization, and mechanistic understanding.
evidence_items.title: Coupling large language models with domain-specific small models: toward efficient extraction, management and validation of 2D materials literature data.

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
Patient experience surveys may contain signals of diagnostic breakdowns that are difficult to identify through conventional safety surveillance. Natural language processing (NLP) may enable these narratives to be analyzed at scale.


OBJECTIVE
To develop and evaluate three increasingly context-sensitive NLP approaches for identifying patient-perceived diagnostic breakdowns in ambulatory patient experience survey comments and to explore the potential of prompt-engineered large language models (LLMs) for this task.


METHODS
We analyzed 523 free-text comments from a 2023 ambulatory patient experience survey at a Canadian academic community hospital. Comments were manually coded using a structured framework to establish a finalized reference standard. Three sequential approaches were developed: a TF-IDF-based XGBoost classifier (Phase I), a fine-tuned Twitter-RoBERTa model (Phase II), and a locally deployed LLaMA 3.3 70B model refined through iterative expert-guided prompt development (Phase III). Phases I and II were evaluated using 5×5 nested stratified cross-validation. Phase III was refined and evaluated on the full dataset and therefore represents development-set rather than independent held-out performance.


RESULTS
Following expert review, 51 of 523 comments (9.8%) were classified as diagnostic breakdowns. Compared with Phase I, Phase II showed higher recall (0.767 vs 0.626), F1 score (0.620 vs 0.548), AUROC (0.921 vs 0.810), and AUPRC (0.564 vs 0.490). In Phase III, iterative prompt refinement reduced over-classification of general experiential complaints. The final prompt achieved recall of 0.961, precision of 0.803, specificity of 0.975, and an F1 score of 0.875 on the development dataset.


CONCLUSIONS
Patient-authored survey narratives are an underused source of information for diagnostic safety and quality improvement. Context-sensitive NLP approaches may improve detection of subtle diagnostic concerns, and the strong development-set performance of the prompt-engineered LLM supports further study. External validation and prospective evaluation within diagnostic-safety workflows are needed before broader implementation.


CLINICALTRIAL
evidence_items.title: Identifying Diagnostic Breakdowns in Patient Experience Survey Comments Using Natural Language Processing: An Evaluation Study.

evidence_items.summary: Objective: To evaluate large language model (LLM) generation of type 2 diabetes (T2DM) phenotyping SQL and the effect of database implementation context. Materials and Methods: Eight publicly accessible LLM-based systems generated SQL under progressively richer prompts using synthetic and University of North Carolina (UNC) Health electronic health record (EHR) data, both based on the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) model. Outputs were compared with the Electronic Medical Records and Genomics (eMERGE) T2DM reference phenotype using SQL executability, F1, positive predictive value (PPV), and recall. Results: Fewer than 55% of limited-context synthetic outputs and no limited-context UNC EHR outputs executed without modification. Detailed codebooks (L3) increased executability to 81.3% in synthetic OMOP and 100% in UNC EHR; adding sample rows (L4) increased synthetic executability to 100%. Limited-context recall was as low as 0.01, whereas high-context outputs achieved recall [≥]0.99 at synthetic L4 and >0.90 at UNC L3, although UNC PPV remained substantially lower than recall. At the highest available context levels, Beta F1 ranged from 0.72-0.99 in synthetic OMOP and 0.57-0.68 in UNC EHR; all UNC models exceeded the diagnosis-code baseline (F1=0.54). The top synthetic performer fell from F1=0.99 to 0.64 on UNC EHR. Discussion: Richer database context was associated with more consistent SQL executability and recall, while model rankings varied across datasets. Conclusion: LLMs can generate clinically meaningful T2DM phenotyping SQL when provided with sufficient database context, but limited PPV in real-world data underscores the need for local validation.
evidence_items.title: Richer database context improves LLM-generated EHR phenotyping algorithms

evidence_items.summary: Transformer-based architectures have revolutionized Question Answering (QA), yet navigating the trade-off between architectural complexity, computational efficiency, and robust generalization remains a critical challenge. This study presents a rigorous, side-by-side evaluation of four distinct Transformer models—ALBERT, RoBERTa, DeBERTa, and XLNet—on the SQuAD v2.0 benchmark, which demands both precise span extraction and calibration to abstain from unanswerable queries. By employing identical preprocessing pipelines and hyperparameter schedules, we isolate the impact of specific architectural innovations, including dynamic masking, disentangled attention, and permutation language modeling. Experimental results establish RoBERTa as the performance leader (85.90% EM, 88.69% F1), validating the efficacy of robust optimization strategies. Notably, DeBERTa followed closely (85.41% EM, 88.54% F1) but achieved superior performance on unanswerable questions (88.24%), suggesting that its disentangled attention mechanism offers enhanced verification capabilities against distractor entities. XLNet demonstrated competitive potential (78.30% EM) via its autoregressive formulation, while ALBERT confirmed its status as the efficiency benchmark, delivering respectable accuracy (80.70% EM) with a fraction of the parameter footprint. Qualitative error analysis reveals that while lighter models are prone to "hallucinating" answers, advanced architectures primarily fail due to subtle reasoning errors rather than entity mismatch. These findings provide a definitive decision framework for practitioners: prioritizing RoBERTa and DeBERTa for maximum reliability in complex domains, and leveraging ALBERT for scalable, resource-constrained deployments.
evidence_items.title: Comparative Analysis of Transformer-Based Models for Question Answering on SQuAD v2.0

evidence_items.summary: Benchmarks such as WildfireSpreadTS (WSTS) have enabled data-driven forecasting of wildfire spread from multimodal satellite time series, but they suffer from limitations: size restricts them to large fires that burn for weeks, and they are from similar environments. We introduce AFSeq, a multimodal dataset of 1,194 recent fire events (2023 to 2026) from 8 different countries across three regions, dominated by the short, small fires that existing benchmarks underrepresent. Our dataset is the largest and most diverse to date for time-series-based wildfire spread prediction. We also introduce UTAE-AR, an extension of a classical U-Net with Temporal Auto Encoder, enhanced with recurrent modules before the decoder. This allows the model to not only predict the next day but the whole sequence in an autoregressive way. Moreover, our model can feed its own predicted fire mask back one day at a time, producing the day-by-day forecasts that single-step models cannot. Our results show that UTAE-AR surpasses state-of-the-art on both WSTS, WSTS+ and AFSeq for next-day accuracy while having 21.5% of their parameters, and being able to predict confidently at a longer horizon.
evidence_items.title: From Next Day Wildfire to Next Days Wildfire: A New Multi-Continent Dataset of Active-Fire Spread for Sequence-to-Sequence Forecasting

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Background Varian machine performance check (MPC) is a manufacturer integrated quality control system included as standard for TrueBeam and Halcyon linear accelerators (linacs) to assess performance using a broad range of geometric and beam tests. MPC is a highly standardized method of performance testing, is generally free of inter‐user variability and is quick and easy to perform allowing daily acquisitions. Therefore, previous studies have highlighted the potential of comparative analysis of MPC data in investigating differences in performance of individual linacs and identifying outliers. Statistical process control (SPC) is an established approach commonly used to assess stability and behavior of sequential data and identify standard operating ranges which has previously been applied to radiotherapy quality assurance data and MPC data. Purpose This study aimed to investigate the feasibility of a web‐based platform using SPC and aggregated MPC data to allow users to compare their machine performance against that of a cohort of others in the radiotherapy community. Methods A previously developed web‐based platform for radiotherapy data sharing was expanded to include the MPC data collection and comparison tool. Pilot centers exported data from their MPC applications and uploaded it through center‐specific portals. Within the application, SPC analysis was used to calculate upper control limits (UCL), lower control limits (LCL) and central lines (CL) for the data sets of each individual linac as well as cohort averages. Interactive plots of longitudinal data for individual machines were displayed for users and overlaid with SPC limits for the specific machine and the cohort averages. Additional analyses were conducted externally from the app where the average and range of SPC control limits for the cohort were compared against MPC tolerances. Results MPC data for 57 648 measurements taken between April 2016 and May 2026 were collected across seven centers from 21 TrueBeam linacs (15 with Millennium multi‐leaf collimator (MLC), six with HD120 MLCs) and one Halcyon. Variation in performance for specific tests was identified for individual machines compared against the cohort as well as for individual MLC leaves for specific machines. Across the cohort of TrueBeam linacs, average control ranges for all geometric tests were within MPC thresholds. However, the range of values for UCL and LCL exceeded tolerances for relative gantry angle. Machines installed before 2021 were found to have slightly larger variability in mean MLC offset with an average control range width of 0.20 mm and 0.18 mm for bank A and B, respectively, compared to machines installed after 2021 of 0.10 mm and 0.13 mm. Analysis of data for individual linacs segmented per year showed a change in mean MLC offset occurring around 2021. Conclusions The usefulness and feasibility of a tool to compare MPC data against the radiotherapy community was demonstrated. Inter‐center comparison of data allowed trends to be identified which would otherwise not be observable for individual centers. Further development and distribution of the MPC data sharing and comparison tool may provide improved confidence and understanding of machine performance and assist low‐resourced clinics in delivering safe and accurate radiotherapy treatments.
evidence_items.title: Linac performance benchmarking: Feasibility of a web‐based tool for comparison of local machine performance check (MPC) results with the global community

evidence_items.summary:
MOTIVATION
Drug-drug interaction (DDI) prediction is critical for drug safety, yet existing methods suffer from structural incompleteness in drug representation. Motif and molecular graph encodings capture local substructures and global topology but remain confined to the closed structural space of individual molecules, lacking cross-entity and contextual information and leading to limited generalization, especially in cold-start scenarios. To address this issue, we propose CSK-DDI, a multimodal framework that jointly encodes motif-level chemical patterns, molecular graph topology, and biomedical knowledge graph context as complementary drug representations. The KG encodes drugs' contextual positions and relational semantics through multi-entity and multi-relation connections, providing global cross-entity and cross-semantic information that complements structural representations. The resulting fusion captures local chemical patterns, global topology, and biomedical context in a unified embedding.


RESULTS
CSK-DDI employs a cross-attention mechanism to enable multi-view interaction among motif, molecular graph, and knowledge graph representations, producing unified structure-aware and context-aware drug embeddings. To improve robustness under sparse conditions, the model further incorporates a cold-start-oriented representation enhancement strategy. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods, with particularly notable gains in cold-start scenarios.


AVAILABILITY
Source code and data are available at https://github.com/cgwcbz2/CSK-DDI and on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21415769.


SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION
Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
evidence_items.title: CSK-DDI: Compensating Structural Incompleteness with Knowledge Graph World Knowledge for Drug-Drug Interaction Modeling.

evidence_items.summary: Chagas disease (CD), caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, is a significant public health challenge in Latin America, where an estimated 70% of infected individuals remain undiagnosed. Rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) offer a promising solution for new screening strategies, yet their performance has not been systematically assessed in Mexican cohorts. Here, we evaluated the diagnostic performance of five RDTs: Chagas Rapid Test (Certum), Bio-Chagas Rapid Test (Mexlab), BiolineTM Chagas Ab (Abbott), Chagas Rapid Test (Amunet) and Chagas Sero K-SeT (Coris BioConcept). Performance was tested using 79 archived human serum samples from Yucatan. All tests were benchmarked against the diagnostic reference algorithm established by the Mexican Official Norm (NOM), where samples were characterised as positive if they were reactive to [≥] 2 conventional serological assays (Chagatest Lisado, Chagatest Recombinante v4.0 and Chagatest HAI). The RDTs demonstrated variable diagnostic sensitivity. The BiolineTM Chagas Ab test demonstrated the highest sensitivity (97.2%, 95% CI: 85.5 - 99.9; 35/36 positive samples detected) and almost perfect statistical agreement with the NOM reference algorithm ({kappa}= 0.90; p < 0.0001). Similarly, the Chagas Sero K-SeT prototype showed a high sensitivity (91.7%, 95% CI: 77.5 - 98.2; 33/36 positive samples detected) and substantial concordance ({kappa}= 0.87, p < 0.0001) with the NOM-based composite result. In contrast, the remaining RDTs demonstrated low sensitivities (Certum: 0.0%, 95% CI: 0.0-9.7; Mexlab: 5.6%, 95% CI: 0.7-18.7; Amunet: 33.3%, 95% CI: 18.6-51.0), limiting their suitability for CD diagnostic algorithms, at least in Yucatan. Specificity was consistently high across the RDTs, ranging from 93.0% to 100% (95% CIs: 80.9-100). These findings underscore the need to locally validate diagnostic tools. The BiolineTM Chagas Ab and Chagas Sero K-SeT tests met the WHO benchmarks for RDT performance and, if validated in larger cohorts, could strengthen the screening of T. cruzi infection and epidemiological surveillance in Mexico.
evidence_items.title: Laboratory evaluation of five rapid diagnostic tests for the serological diagnosis of chronic Trypanosoma cruzi infection in Yucatan, Mexico

evidence_items.summary: We introduce The Prestige, a video understanding benchmark that probes cognitive visual reasoning through professional magic performances, where deliberate misdirection challenges models to track events and explain unexpected outcomes. The benchmark comprises open-ended questions ranging from temporal and causal understanding to robustness against adversarial questions. Evaluation of leading open-source and proprietary VLMs reveals a substantial gap between even the strongest model and human performance. We also find systematic discrepancies between human and automated grading and identify recurring model failure modes. Ablations further show that models can select correct multiple-choice answers even when they fail to generate correct explanations independently, motivating further investigations into question formats. Together, these findings highlight limitations in both VLM reasoning and its evaluation, underscoring the need for more reliable video understanding models and more rigorous benchmarks.
evidence_items.title: The Prestige: Benchmarking Cognitive Visual Reasoning using Magic Tricks

evidence_items.summary: Background: Mathematical coupling and comparator selection are established concerns when a transcriptome response is defined as follow-up minus baseline. We assessed whether apparent within-cohort improvement survives matched constant-follow-up and scalar-shrinkage controls, and whether specified evaluation faults are detectable in an auditable vascular transcriptome benchmark. Results: Using eight frozen modules, 72 rosuvastatin pairs, 14 peripheral artery disease pairs, 20 repeated subject-held-out five-fold partitions, and 5,000 subject bootstrap draws of fixed losses, we compared 15 explicit specifications. Supporting post hoc analyses included 800 known-truth training/test simulations, annotation and input-ablation sensitivities, complete-tuning integrity checks, and an independent-source cross-sectional artery description. In GSE86216, nested follow-up ridge had lower observed repeated-CV mean absolute error than mean follow-up, 0.3280 versus 0.3405 (difference 0.0126; descriptive central 95% percentile range 0.0033-0.0224), while scalar shrinkage had lower observed error (0.3256). These ranges have no validated coverage guarantee. No full-matrix advantage was established; equivalence was not tested. In peripheral artery disease, nested ridge (0.3449) had slightly higher observed MAE than the median follow-up comparator (0.3409), and no advantage was established. Simulations illustrated how mean follow-up can outperform mean change without temporal signal, while the GSE281841 histological stenosis-grade description remained limited by anatomical imbalance, unconfirmed participant identity and an unresolved sample-count discrepancy. Conclusions: These retrospective, nonconfirmatory comparisons show modestly lower observed within-cohort error than constant-follow-up controls in one cohort, without established full-matrix advantage. They do not partition prediction into mathematical, technical and biological components. Independent longitudinal validation and clinical utility remain unestablished.
evidence_items.title: VascFlux-GEO: Comparator selection and auditability in vascular transcriptome module prediction

evidence_items.summary: Objective pain assessment is challenging due to the inherently subjective and multidimensional nature of pain, compounded by intersubject variability and noise in naturalistic settings. These factors limit the development of reliable digital biomarkers for clinical decision support and remote monitoring. In this work, we propose a hybrid deep learning architecture that performs early fusion of single channel EEG band power streams with peripheral biosignals recorded by a wristband (electrodermal activity, photoplethysmography/BVP, triaxial accelerometry, and skin temperature). The model uses residual 1D CNN encoders to learn EEG representations and a multilayer perceptron to encode wearable features; the two embeddings are fused in a unified layer to produce predictions for four classes under a strict subject independent evaluation protocol. On PhysioPain, the proposed approach achieves 86.98% accuracy and 87.46% weighted F1, surpassing widely used machine learning baselines, while maintaining an average inference latency of 0.1495 ms per sample for real time operation. In addition to widely used machine learning baselines, we benchmark contemporary deep 1D CNN baselines for a fair comparison: the proposed model improves over 1D DenseNet by 4.49 percentage points in accuracy and 4.70 percentage points in weighted F1, and over 1D ResNet by 7.90 percentage points in accuracy and 7.93 percentage points in weighted F1. To our knowledge, this is the first study to perform subject independent multiclass classification of natural pain phenotypes with explicit handling of class imbalance by early fusion of MindWave EEG with Empatica E4 signals, representing a step toward generalizable and clinically useful digital biomarkers of pain.
evidence_items.title: Multimodal EEG–Wearable Integration for Generalizable Pain Classification

evidence_items.summary: In recent years, warehouse logistics optimization has increasingly focused on intelligent, data-driven systems to enhance operational efficiency. Conventional static product placement strategies are being progressively replaced by dynamic slotting approaches that can adapt to real-time variations in warehouse conditions. In this work, we present a novel framework that employs a reinforcement learning agent integrated within a FlexSim-based Digital Twin environment for real-time product placement optimization. The proposed agent continuously learns from streaming operational data, enabling it to reduce picking time while improving overall system throughput. The simulation environment models a four-zone warehouse layout with forklift-based material handling and leverages the Asset Administration Shell framework to ensure seamless interaction between the learning agent, physical asset, and the digital twin. Experimental evaluation demonstrates substantial performance gains, with the proposed approach achieving a 29.66\% reduction in average picking time, a 35.42\% increase in throughput, and an 18.54\% decrease in travel distance.
evidence_items.title: AI-Driven Digital Twin Framework for Warehouse Logistics Automation Optimization

evidence_items.summary: The emergence of non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs) has significantly transformed the landscape of organic solar cells (OSCs) and paved the way for achieving unprecedented power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) and making them suitable for practical photovoltaic applications. Computational techniques, meanwhile, have become essential for the efficient discovery, screening, and optimization of new photovoltaic (PV) materials. This review gives a comprehensive summary of the recent developments in computational design and construction of NFAs with special attention to the use of computational tools in the understanding and enhancement of the structural, electronic and optoelectronic properties of NFAs. In addition, the challenges related to the stability and degradation of NFAs are briefly addressed, with prominence on how computational methods can contribute to understanding these issues. Furthermore, this review comprehensively evaluates the core computational strategies used to probe NFA degradation mechanisms specifically photostability, thermal stress, morphological evolution and oxidative pathways, and offers computational solutions to improve the long-term stability of OSC devices. As the efficiency of OSCs has approached the benchmark values, the attention towards their practical application has risen substantially. Therefore, the importance of computational techniques like density functional theory (DFT), time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT), machine learning (ML) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations is discussed to highlight the key aspects of NFA performance including charge transport, light harvesting, device stability, and exciton dissociation. Moreover, the role of these computational tools in understanding and predicting the structure–property relationships is described, which helps in the design of new NFA materials with enhanced device performance. Finally, the breakthroughs and future perspectives in the design of NFAs using computational approaches are discussed.
evidence_items.title: A critical review of degradation pathways and stability engineering for high-efficiency non-fullerene acceptor-based organic solar cells via multiscale computational approaches

evidence_items.summary: The widespread presence of antibiotic residues in aquatic environments contributes to ecological toxicity and accelerates antimicrobial resistance (AMR), highlighting the need for efficient and sustainable remediation technologies. Among advanced oxidation processes, TiO2-based photocatalysis has attracted considerable attention because of its chemical stability, low toxicity, and strong oxidative capability. However, the practical application of TiO2 is limited by poor visible-light absorption and rapid electron–hole recombination. Carbon dots (CDs) have emerged as highly promising interfacial modifiers owing to their tunable electronic structure, visible-light responsiveness, and efficient charge-transfer capability, enabling substantial enhancement of TiO2 photocatalytic performance. This review critically examines recent advances in CDs/TiO2 nanocomposites for photocatalytic antibiotic degradation, with particular emphasis on how heterointerface engineering governs charge-carrier dynamics, reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, and degradation selectivity. The mechanistic roles of Ti–O–C interfacial bonding, band alignment, defect-state modulation, and interfacial electron transfer are systematically discussed in relation to photocatalytic activity across major antibiotic classes, including tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, β-lactams, and sulfonamides. In addition, the effects of adsorption behavior, operational parameters, environmental matrix components, and reactor configuration on degradation efficiency and mineralization are critically evaluated. Special attention is devoted to degradation pathways, catalyst photostability, ecotoxicological considerations, and challenges associated with real-water applications and large-scale implementation. Current limitations, including insufficient mechanistic validation, lack of standardized benchmarking protocols, and limited long-term environmental safety assessment, are also highlighted. Finally, current research priorities involving mechanistic validation, predictive interfacial engineering, standardized benchmarking, environmental safety assessment, and solar-driven photocatalytic design are highlighted to guide the future development of sustainable antibiotic-remediation technologies.
evidence_items.title: Carbon dot/TiO2 nanocomposites for photocatalytic antibiotic degradation: interfacial engineering, degradation mechanisms, and environmental remediation

evidence_items.summary: Bone organoids are emerging as three-dimensional skeletal models that reproduce selected aspects of bone development, organization, and function under controlled conditions. Physiologically relevant models require more than cellular aggregation and mineral deposition; they must progressively acquire organized matrices, multicellular interactions, vascular and metabolic support, and mechanical responsiveness. In this review, we examine developmental principles guiding bone-organoid construction, including skeletal hierarchy, cellular niches, ossification pathways, and spatiotemporal signaling. We then discuss current strategies based on skeletal, mesenchymal stromal, and pluripotent stem cells, together with advances in biomaterials, three-dimensional bioprinting, perfusion, and microfluidic culture. To organize these developments, we introduce the development-to-remodeling continuum (DRC), which distinguishes tissue formation from multicellular integration, adaptive responsiveness, and remodeling competence. We assess collagen-mineral organization, osteocyte-network formation, vascular and metabolic maturation, osteoblast-osteoclast coupling, marrow and immune integration, and mechanical adaptation. We further evaluate applications in developmental and disease modeling, drug assessment, personalized modeling, and bone regeneration. Current limitations include variability, incomplete maturation, transport constraints, and insufficient functional benchmarking. By linking construction strategies to specific bone-related functions and the evidence supporting them, the DRC provides a framework for evaluating functional claims in relation to intended application and translational readiness.
evidence_items.title: Bone Organoids Across the Development-to-Remodeling Continuum: From Tissue Formation to Functional Competence and Translation.

evidence_items.summary: Objectives The present study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of extracts from five Cameroonian medicinal plants against planktonic forms of Helicobacter pylori isolates and assessed their ability to inhibit biofilm formation and eradicate preformed biofilms. Methods The antimicrobial activity of 15 extracts obtained from Psidium guajava leaves, Mangifera indica leaves, Cymbopogon citratus aerial parts, Musa ‘False Horn’ ripe fruit peelings, and Syzygium aromaticum flower buds was evaluated against 48 planktonic forms of H. pylori clinical isolates using the broth microdilution method. The inhibition of biofilm formation and eradication of preformed biofilms were evaluated using the crystal violet staining assay. Results The hexane extract of M. indica leaves exhibited the strongest antibacterial activity, with minimum inhibitory concentration values ranging from 31.25 to 62.5 μg/mL against 3/48 (6.25%) of the tested isolates. The lowest minimum biofilm inhibition concentration (MBIC) of 62.5 μg/mL was obtained with the methanol extract of Musa ‘False Horn’ fruit peelings and the dichloromethane extract of P. guajava leaves. The lowest minimum biofilm eradication concentration (MBEC) of 125 μg/mL was recorded for the hexane extract of P. guajava leaves and the methanol extract of Musa ‘False Horn’ fruit peelings. Conclusion The investigated plant extracts exhibited antibacterial activity against planktonic H. pylori, whereas several extracts also demonstrated promising antibiofilm activity. These findings support further phytochemical characterization, toxicity evaluation, and in vivo studies to investigate their potential as complementary therapeutic agents against H. pylori infections.
evidence_items.title: Anti‐Helicobacter pylori Activity of Musa ‘False Horn’ (Musaceae), Syzygium aromaticum (Myrtaceae), Psidium guajava (Myrtaceae), Mangifera indica (Anacardiaceae), and Cymbopogon citratus (Poaceae) and Their Potential to Prevent and Eradicate H. pylori Biofilms

evidence_items.summary: Artifact of the tool paper "A-Ivy: Authoring and Testing Protocol Ivy Specifications from RFCs with Supervised LLMs", submitted to TACAS 2027. The paper measured one frozen snapshot of A-Ivy's five repositories.  You use the artifact as the authors use A-Ivy, and as the paper's Sect. 3 did: you install A-Ivy on your machine (the TACAS 2027 VM, or a Linux or macOS host) from the archive's source, and work with its plugin in Claude Code, on an API key that the AE chairs hold.  You repeat the session that Sect. 3 follows, on the same requirement of RFC 4271 §6.3, up to the test's run against FRRouting, which PANTHER starts in Docker containers on your machine; the authors have not run that last step on this version. Agent runs may differ from run to run, so the results are similar to the paper's, not identical. The archive also holds the recorded evidence of the paper's own runs, and a Docker image of the tool, for amd64 and arm64, that runs its checks with no key and no network. Sources: the release commits of PANTHER, PANTHER-Ivy, panther-ivy-plugin, ivy-lsp and vscode-ivy.

evidence_items.summary: Metabarcoding has become a cornerstone of environmental and biodiversity research, yet much of the value locked in the resulting sequence data is never fully realized: workflows are fragmented across incompatible tools, metadata is inconsistent or missing, and analyses rarely survive reuse beyond the group that produced them. As datasets grow, these bottlenecks undermine the connected, sustainable ecosystem the community is building. O2A SEQUENCES is an open, modular platform that unifies the storage, processing, and analysis of metabarcoding data in an environment designed for sharing and reuse, embedded in the O2A data flow framework developed and operated by the Alfred-Wegener-Institute. Researchers upload raw sequencing data and choose from domain-appropriate workflows for different marker genes, ecosystems, and analytical goals. These workflows are harmonized through AMPBA (Accessible Metabarcoding Platform for Biodiversity Analysis) , a community initiative developing pipelines with biologists for the most common metabarcoding use cases. Integrated quality-control surface data problems early. Metadata is managed through full integration with O2A SAMPLES for harmonized sample metadata, linking to the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) via MIxS and Darwin Core community standards, making outputs interoperable and publication-ready. A working prototype will be publicly available soon. By coupling standardized metadata with portable, open analysis, O2A SEQUENCES turns scattered sequencing efforts into FAIR resources and building blocks for a global open research commons. This directly contributes to the goals of RDA groups such as Biodiversity Data Integration and Life Science Data Infrastructures, which focus on interoperable, standards-based integration and reuse of complex biological datasets across domains and infrastructures. Lars Harms, Alexey Savchik, Roland Koppe and Sonja Hänzelmann (shared authors) Presented at RDA P27
evidence_items.title: O2A SEQUENCES: A Modular, Reproducible Platform for End-to-End Metabarcoding Data Management

evidence_items.summary: Direct Contact Membrane Distillation (DCMD) was investigated for water and heat reuse from steel industry wastewater, with a novel integrated framework combining experimental validation, thermodynamic simulations, and predictive modelling. Experimental tests with a hollow fiber polypropylene membrane demonstrated stable flux in the range of 1.4–4.8 kg/(m² h) over a feed temperature range of 40–60 °C, with salt rejection above 99.9% and no evidence of scaling or wetting, even up to 93% recovery. Then, solubility simulations with PHREEQC were performed, accurately reproducing solution properties and predicting undersaturation conditions even at high recoveries. The constant and high water activity calculated from these simulations explains the stable flux observed, while the predicted absence of solid phases matches the lack of scaling in experiments. The developed DCMD model was validated against experimental data and 14 independent datasets from the literature, achieving low errors ( MAPE < 5%) and strong correlations ( R² > 0.96) for flux and outlet temperatures. Parametric simulations revealed that higher feed temperatures and velocities enhance flux, productivity and specific thermal energy consumption (STEC), while reducing the membrane area required to produce 1 m³/day of water. These improvements result from increased driving force and reduced polarization effects but must be balanced against higher energy demands for heating and pumping. Overall, the study demonstrates that DCMD can achieve high recovery and excellent water quality for industrial wastewater treatment, and that the validated model provides a reliable tool for system design and scale-up in industrial contexts.
evidence_items.title: Sustainable water recovery from steel industry wastewater via direct contact membrane distillation

evidence_items.summary: The dataset contains data from an online expert panel on barriers to the digitalisation of organisations in Slovakia, conducted in 2026 as part of the Overcoming Digital Divide in Europe and Southeast Asia (ODDEA) project (Horizon Europe, Grant Agreement No. 101086381). The panel addressed the main barriers to digital transformation, possible measures to overcome them, and future challenges. The dataset includes coded records of the discussion, the participants’ individual prioritisation of predefined barriers, and written expert input. The dataset is pseudonymised: participants are identified by codes, and personal identifiers were removed or generalised. Supporting records on attendance and consent are not part of the dataset; they are held by the EUBA research team on the university’s institutional storage (MS OneDrive), with access restricted to members of the EUBA research team, and are not shared with ODDEA consortium partners.

evidence_items.summary: Automatically generated vector design elements must combine visual quality, structural validity, and practical editing capabilities to support professional design workflows. This article examines artificial intelligence methods for producing scalable vector graphics, with particular attention to icons and simple decorative elements. A targeted qualitative review of sixteen scientific publications, supported by the SVG specification, compares learned vector representations, differentiable rendering and optimization, and autoregressive SVG generation. The studies are analysed according to their conditioning inputs, output representations, control mechanisms, and implications for evaluation. The synthesis indicates that visual similarity, file validity, and editability must be assessed separately. Differentiable rendering connects image-based objectives to vector parameters, whereas token-based approaches generate structured commands or SVG code directly. On this basis, the article proposes a workflow that separates mandatory structural and palette checks from subsequent ranking by semantic relevance, style consistency, and geometric complexity. A prospective evaluation protocol is specified for comparing alternative selection policies on the same candidate pool, using held-out prompts, independent expert assessments, and timed editing tasks. The article reports a methodological synthesis and an evaluation design; it does not report newly executed model experiments or measured performance improvements. The workflow provides a basis for investigating whether explicit constraints improve the usability of generated vector assets.
evidence_items.title: VECTOR APPROACHES TO THE AUTOMATIC GENERATION OF GRAPHIC DESIGN ELEMENTS USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE

evidence_items.summary: This study examines the primary determinants of CPI-adjusted monthly producer egg prices in India from January 2013 through December 2025. The analysis uses 156 monthly observations constructed from daily National Egg Coordination Committee city-level egg-price quotations. Explanatory variables include CPI-adjusted World Bank maize and soybean-meal benchmark prices, domestic diesel prices, a COVID-19-period indicator, a linear trend, and calendar-month fixed effects. Ordinary least squares regression models were estimated sequentially to assess the contribution of each group of variables. Models containing only feed prices, diesel prices, the COVID indicator, and trend explained little of the variation in producer egg prices, with the highest pre-seasonality R-squared equal to .046. The inclusion of month fixed effects substantially improved model performance: the final model explained 63.8% of monthly variation in CPI-adjusted producer egg prices, with an adjusted R-squared of .596. Producer egg prices were significantly lower than January prices in most months between February and October, with the largest reduction occurring in April. December prices were significantly higher than January prices. These results indicate that recurring seasonal variation is the dominant observed correlate of monthly producer egg-price movements. Among the non-seasonal variables, soybean meal was positively and statistically significantly associated with producer egg prices. Maize, diesel, the COVID-period indicator, and the linear trend were not statistically significant after controlling for seasonality and the other covariates. The findings should be interpreted as conditional associations rather than causal effects because the study uses aggregated observational data, global feed-price benchmarks rather than domestic farm-level feed prices, and a level-regression framework with mixed stationarity properties.
evidence_items.title: Explaining Indian Egg Price Dynamics: Seasonal Patterns, Feed Costs, and Diesel Prices, 2013–2025

evidence_items.summary: This study examines the effectiveness of Task-Based Language Teaching (TBLT) in fostering critical thinking skills among intermediate-level English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners. A quasi-experimental design was employed with 64 intermediate EFL students randomly assigned to an experimental group (n = 32) that received TBLT instruction and a control group (n = 32) that followed a conventional presentation-practice-production approach over a 12-week period. Critical thinking was measured using a modified California Critical Thinking Skills Test adapted for language learners and a task-based performance rubric assessing analysis, evaluation, inference, and argumentation. Results indicated statistically significant gains in the experimental group across all critical thinking dimensions (p < .01), with particularly strong improvements in analysis and evaluation. Qualitative data from learner reflective journals and classroom observations further revealed that authentic, meaning-focused tasks encouraged deeper cognitive engagement, perspective-taking, and reasoned decision-making. The findings suggest that carefully designed TBLT sequences can simultaneously advance linguistic competence and higher-order thinking skills. Implications for EFL curriculum design and teacher training are discussed.
evidence_items.title: DEVELOPING CRITICAL THINKING SKILLS IN INTERMEDIATE EFL LEARNERS THROUGH TASK-BASED LANGUAGE TEACHING
Performance Evaluation of Embedded AI Inference on Zynq Ultrascale+ and Versal SoCs for Onboard Space Applications

evidence_items.summary: We study risk-averse decision making, in which an agent selects actions while being uncertain about the true system state. The risk is measured via optimized certainty equivalent (OCE) metrics, which generalize popular criteria such as mean-variance risk and conditional value-at-risk (CVaR). We characterize the optimal policy under known distributions, and show that it reduces to a prediction set-based solution for the CVaR. This provides an operational interpretation of conformal prediction-type prediction sets. For unknown distributions, we develop a data-driven calibration strategy, based on a synthetic model for the likelihood and held-out calibration data, yielding high-probability control of the OCE risk. The approach is evaluated on two wireless beamforming settings.
evidence_items.title: Conformal Risk-Averse Decision Making with Optimized Certainty Equivalent Risk Control

evidence_items.summary: Deploying trustworthy AI systems requires principled uncertainty quantification. Conformal prediction (CP) is a widely used framework for constructing prediction sets with distribution-free coverage guarantees. In many practical settings, including healthcare, finance, and mobile sensing, the calibration data required for CP are distributed across multiple clients, each with its own local data distribution. In this federated setting, data can often be partitioned into, potentially overlapping, groups, which may reflect client-specific strata or cross-cutting attributes such as demographic or semantic categories. We propose group-conditional federated conformal prediction (GC-FCP), a federated extension of conditional conformal calibration for a target mixture over prespecified groups. GC-FCP constructs mergeable, atom-stratified coresets from local calibration scores, enabling compact aggregation at the server when the number of active atoms is moderate. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets validate the performance of GC-FCP compared to centralized calibration baselines. The code of our work can be found at https://github.com/HaifengWen/GC-FCP.
evidence_items.title: Efficient Federated Conformal Prediction with Group-Conditional Guarantee

evidence_items.summary: A comparative assessment of documented agroforestry water management systems reveals recurring functional limitations in commonly applied Keyline-inspired designs. Observable indicators of concentrated surface runoff, erosion, and insufficient overflow stability can be identified through field- and image-based assessments. A preliminary functional evaluation framework is proposed to support the assessment and design of water management systems in agroforestry.
evidence_items.title: Re-evaluating Keyline Design: Towards Functional Water Management in Agroforestry Systems
