evidence_items.summary: Abstract We present a Bayesian framework, Two-stage Inference for Light curve DEcomposition ( TILDE ), for mapping the accretion disk and the broad-line region (BLR) from active galactic nucleus (AGN) multiband light curves. By inferring delayed BLR contamination from the underlying disk variability, TILDE provides the delay measurements of the disk as well as the BLR. We validate TILDE using synthetic data, finding that TILDE recovers the known time delays of the disk and BLR. By applying TILDE to the Seoul National University AGN Monitoring Project sample, we find that the inferred BLR light curves match the observed H β emission light curves, providing consistent BLR lags compared to the reported H β lags. Using the lag spectrum, effectively corrected for the BLR contamination, we find that the disk size is broadly consistent with the standard thin-disk model, suggesting that BLR contamination can significantly bias the disk size derived from the cross-correlation analysis of the broadband photometry. These results demonstrate that the new inference method is a powerful tool for determining both disk and BLR sizes from broadband photometry in the era of time-domain surveys.
evidence_items.title: Unveiling Accretion-disk Reverberation beneath Broad-line Region Contamination with TILDE

evidence_items.summary: This study quantifies the mechanical degradation caused by locally introduced rubber-glove contamination in stress-relieved PBF-LB/M Ti-6Al-4V. Rubber-glove fragments were inserted into defined build layers of standardized tensile specimens and into highly loaded transition regions of a topology-optimized bracket demonstrator. Twelve uncontaminated and twelve contaminated tensile specimens and nine brackets per condition were evaluated. The contaminated tensile specimens exhibited a mean ultimate strength of approx. 860 MPa compared with approx. 1200 MPa for the reference condition, corresponding to a reduction of approx. 28%. Mean elongation at break decreased from approx. 13.4% to 0.6%, representing a reduction of approx. 95%. Fracture preferentially occurred at the contamination insertion region and was associated with planar fracture features and retained spherical powder particles. The results support a predominantly defect-controlled degradation mechanism associated with locally disturbed consolidation.
evidence_items.title: Mechanical Degradation and Fracture Behavior of PBF-LB/M Ti-6Al-4V Induced by Rubber-Glove Contamination

evidence_items.summary: Abstract As traditional pollution risk assessments fail to comprehensively consider the conbined effects of individual element toxicity and pollutant species, a modified geoaccumulation index ( I geo ) was proposed to identify priority trace metals and assess pollution risk characteristics in agricultural soils at a rural–urban interface area. Seventy agricultural soil samples were collected and analyzed for 6 heavy metals (Cr, Ni, Cu, Zn, Cd, Pb). To account for uncertainty from spatial heterogeneity in soil heavy metals and model parameters in the risk assessment model, a health risk model coupled with probabilistic triangular fuzzy numbers (TFN) was utilized to evaluate human health risks from three primary exposure pathways. The average concentrations of Cr, Ni, Cu, Zn, Cd, and Pb (mg kg −1 ) were 75.3, 22.6, 44.0, 189, 0.63, and 106, respectively, indicating elevated accumulation of Cd and Pb. The proposed I geo index determined elevated pollution risk levels comparable to the conventional index. Notably, Cd was identified as a priority trace metal to control due to its severe contamination risk ( I m = 3.3). The health risk model revealed no significant non-carcinogenic or cancer risk for adults. However, health risk for children were determined to be unacceptable, with a hazard index (HI) value > 1.0 and a total carcinogenic risk (TCR) > 1.0E−04. Ingestion was identified as the primary pathway of exposure to soil heavy metals. The TFN-based probabilistic assessment indicated higher cancer risk for children than the deterministic method. This difference may be attributed to Cr, which has moderate spatial variability and contributes substantially to health risk. This study provides new insights into pollution and human health risk from soil heavy metals, which can be used to generate strategies to prioritize decision-making on soil heavy metal pollution remediation and risk management in soil environments.
evidence_items.title: Heavy metal contamination and risk assessment with uncertainty analysis in agricultural soils at a rural–urban interface

evidence_items.summary: Autonomous artificial intelligence agents are transforming the practice of science. Across every discipline, researchers are handing data analysis to coding agents that can design and execute complex studies from a single prompt. Yet this revolution carries a threat. When agents improvise in local environments, they leave no verifiable record, ultimately risking a wave of irreproducible science. Solving this crisis requires moving agentic science onto public infrastructure where every action leaves an examinable trail. Here we connect autonomous coding agents to shared computing resources, turning ephemeral prompts into auditable scientific records. After showing that 30 unguided local agents splinter into 18 incompatible pipelines on the same dataset, we conduct an agentic reproduction and discovery study on a large scale---reproducing a large, diverse array of studies with every workflow, history, and intermediate dataset publicly accessible. This complete provenance trail exposes unstated modeling choices, reference mismatches, and subsampled tutorial inputs in published studies, and establishes a new foundation where human scientists can understand, steer, and trust AI-driven discovery.
evidence_items.title: Verifiable Agentic Science on Public Infrastructure

evidence_items.summary: ABSTRACT The pharmaceutical sector is undergoing considerable transformation as a result of the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), automation, robotics, and advanced computing technologies. Traditional pharmaceutical discovery and development processes can be lengthy, costly, and associated with high failure rates, thereby necessitating more efficient approaches. Agentic artificial intelligence (Agentic AI) combines autonomous decision‐making, goal‐oriented reasoning, adaptive learning, and multi‐step task execution. These capabilities may increase the autonomy and coordination of pharmaceutical research workflows. At the same time, self‐driving or autonomous laboratories that utilize robotics, machine learning, laboratory automation, and real‐time data analytics to conduct experiments with minimal or no human intervention have emerged as an alternative approach. Agentic AI can provide a higher‐level orchestration layer for autonomous laboratories, while established approaches such as Bayesian optimization, active learning, machine learning, and robotic experimentation provide many of the underlying capabilities required for closed‐loop experimentation. These technologies can be applied to drug discovery, lead optimization, formulation development, process optimization, and personalized medicine. Several challenges related to data quality, transparency, regulation, cybersecurity, ethical considerations, and infrastructure must be addressed before these systems can be widely adopted. In addition, current evidence is dominated by computational studies, research‐scale proof‐of‐concept platforms, and early industrial implementations. Substantial uncertainty remains regarding their reproducibility, scalability, and effects on overall drug development timelines.
evidence_items.title: The Rise of Agentic AI and Self‐Driving Laboratories: Reshaping Drug Discovery, Development, and Precision Medicine

evidence_items.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are vulnerable to visual jailbreak attacks that bypass safety safeguards. Existing methods typically optimize isolated adversarial examples, limiting attack diversity, transferability, and generalization. We propose Jailbreak Connectivity (JC), a framework based on the observation that effective adversarial inputs can be connected through low-loss regions in image space. JC optimizes continuous adversarial paths: path sampling yields diverse jailbreak images, lightweight surrogate classifiers guide cross-model transfer, and a distribution-level objective enables universal attacks across harmful queries. On MM-SafetyBench, JC achieves average attack success rates of 84.01%, 85.77%, and 97.95% on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, InternVL3.5-8B, and Gemma-3-12B-IT, respectively, exceeding the strongest baselines by up to 68.36 percentage points. In black-box evaluations, JC improves attack success rates over FigStep by 24.69 and 27.34 percentage points on GPT-5.6 and Gemini 3.1 Pro, respectively. These findings reveal structured vulnerabilities in MLLM safety alignment and inform more comprehensive security evaluation.
evidence_items.title: Jailbreak Connectivity: Towards Diverse, Transferable, and Universal Multimodal Large Language Model Jailbreak
Diagnostic and Triage Performance of Large Language Models in Hand and Wrist Complaints: A Standardised Vignette Evaluation.

evidence_items.summary: Peer review is the principal quality control of published research, but methodological errors can go undetected. In an earlier experiment with errors inserted into three reports of randomized clinical trials, untrained human reviewers achieved a mean major-error detection score of 27%. Here, we tested whether 15 large language models (LLMs), including four open-weight models, detect the same errors. Their major-error detection scores ranged from 53% to 96%. To reduce the risk of memorization, we repeated the test on three clinical trials published in 2026. Scores ranged from 51% to 99%, and from 66% to 87% for the open-weight models. Notably, LLMs still flagged 2% to 29% of the error types in control reports without inserted errors, most often conclusions not supported by the results and missing reasons why screened patients were not enrolled. Across the 12 models, mean review times ranged from 1.4 to 16.3 minutes. Opus 5.5 achieved the highest major-error detection score (99%), while GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna offered cost-effective alternatives with scores of 92% and 87%, respectively. Together, these tests provide a benchmark for specialized review models and suggest that relying on human peer review alone may leave avoidable methodological errors undetected.
evidence_items.title: Large language models detect methodological errors that human peer review misses in clinical trials

evidence_items.summary: When a language model returns engineering quantities with the status"solved", software that trusts it passes them on, even when the requested design is physically impossible. Such failures could reflect poor calculation, how the answer is requested, or a failure to judge feasibility. We set beam loads and disk speeds at known percentages above or below plastic collapse or burst, measured each model's limit calculation separately and tested 12 models in 4,860 calls, including follow-up experiments on new designs. We find that a model can recognize an impossible design when asked only whether it is feasible, yet accept the same design, reporting"solved", when asked for a full answer. Three models accepted beams 10 to 30% beyond collapse despite precise limit calculations in separate questions, and many accepted replies stated the violation. Asked only about feasibility, Opus 5 and Gemini 3.8 Flash rejected every impossible new design they were given, including those accepted in full answers, without false alarms. Rewording when to decline or changing the answer format raised rejection on the original beams, but not consistently on new designs. Software and benchmarks using a model's status should test feasibility judgment and full-answer rejection separately, and report the exact prompt.
evidence_items.title: Calculation and rejection diverge in language models tested at known mechanical limits

evidence_items.summary: Conventional artificial intelligence (AI) models can remain overconfident when their predictions are unreliable, limiting clinical adoption. Uncertainty quantification (UQ) supplements predictions with information about confidence, but the literature is often mathematically dense and difficult to translate into action. In this clinically oriented review, we synthesize current evidence and offer a practical perspective on the deployment of uncertainty-aware AI. We describe how uncertainty arises, summarize four principal computational approaches, and examine applications across clinical tasks, model development, foundation models, large language models, and agentic workflows. Uncertainty estimates may identify outputs requiring review, but they do not independently establish safety; their value depends on validation against relevant errors and linkage to appropriate actions in the intended setting. We, therefore, propose an adaptable roadmap connecting local reliability evaluation and threshold selection with subgroup assessment, prospective clinical evaluation, ongoing monitoring, and governance.
evidence_items.title: Moving beyond overconfidence: A clinical roadmap for integrating uncertainty-aware AI models into medical workflows.
A framework for classifying company webpages in business research: evaluating conventional ML against few-shot LLMs

evidence_items.summary: Background Large language models (LLMs) are used at an increased frequency by patients to answer health related questions. Prior studies have evaluated LLMs and their performance with musculoskeletal (MSK) and spine domains, but have not been used to evaluate chiropractic-relevant content. Objective To evaluate ChatGPT responses to commonly asked chiropractic patient questions for concordance with chiropractic clinical practice guidelines. Methods Thirty questions addressing low back pain, neck pain, and chronic musculoskeletal pain were developed based on current U.S. chiropractic clinical practice guidelines (CPGs). ChatGPT (GPT-5.2) generated responses in isolated sessions. Responses were assessed for readability using established indices, then five licensed chiropractors independently rated each response using a 5-point Likert scale across four domains: relevance, clarity, completeness, and accuracy. Inter-rater reliability was evaluated using Krippendorffs alpha (ordinal). Results Readability measures demonstrated that ChatGPT responses were written at approximately a college-level reading grade. Expert ratings across all domain means (standard deviation) were predominately clustered at the upper end of rating scale (1-5): Relevance 4.72 {+/-} 0.56; Clarity 4.76 {+/-} 0.50; Completeness 4.23 {+/-} 0.81; Accuracy 4.00 {+/-} 1.02. The Krippendorffs alpha (ordinal) ranged from -0.023-0.214 across the domains, all reflective of poor inter-rater reliability. Conclusion ChatGPT responses were broadly consistent with chiropractic CPGs, though readability levels exceeded recommended patient education standards. While the expert panel frequently assigned similar scores, minor scoring differences and restricted score distributions produced low chance-corrected reliability. These findings suggest that ChatGPT can produce guideline concordant responses but readability and interpretive variability should be considered when integrating LLM generated information into patient education.
evidence_items.title: Evaluating ChatGPTs Responses to Chiropractic Patient Questions: A Comparative Study

evidence_items.summary:
INTRODUCTION
Geriatric assessment (GA) can identify clinically relevant vulnerabilities in older adults, but remains underused because of time, staffing, and workflow barriers. Conversational artificial intelligence (AI) may provide a scalable approach to support geriatric screening within clinical practice.


MATERIALS AND METHODS
We conducted a two-phase mixed-methods feasibility study evaluating Geriatric Risk Assessment and Capability Evaluation (GRACE), a conversational AI platform for selected structured Practical Geriatric Assessment (PGA)-based screening items, compared with manual PGA assessment. Seventy adults aged ≥65 years were recruited from an academic health system and affiliated community sites. Phase 1 (n = 46) informed platform development and refinement, and Phase 2 (n = 24) evaluated the refined platform. Screening performance was evaluated at the scored-item level using sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, Cohen's κ, and Gwet's AC1. Usability was measured with the System Usability Scale (SUS) and semi-structured interviews with participants and clinicians explored acceptability and implementation.


RESULTS
In Phase 1 (n = 46), GRACE demonstrated sensitivity of 0.68, specificity of 0.96, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 0.96. Following platform refinement, Phase 2 (n = 24) demonstrated sensitivity of 0.77, specificity of 0.97, positive predictive value of 0.72, NPV of 0.98, Cohen's κ of 0.72, and Gwet's AC1 of 0.94. Phase 2 represented the primary estimate of refined-platform performance; overall Phase 1-to-Phase 2 differences were numerical rather than statistically significant. Descriptively pooled across all 70 participants, sensitivity was 0.71, specificity 0.96, NPV 0.97, κ 0.65, and AC1 0.92. Performance varied across domains, with stronger performance in several structured domains and lower sensitivity in functional and psychosocial domains. Participants generally reported favorable usability, and patient and clinician interviews supported a potential role for GRACE in pre-visit information gathering and targeted clinician follow-up.


DISCUSSION
The refined GRACE platform demonstrated promising performance for structured geriatric screening, including high specificity and NPV, supporting its potential role in pre-visit screening and prioritization of clinician follow-up. GRACE should be used as a clinician-guided, human-in-the-loop screening tool rather than as a standalone method for excluding geriatric deficits because GRACE showed lower sensitivity in some domains and NPV depends on prevalence. Larger prospective studies are needed to validate the refined platform and evaluate its implementation and clinical impact.
evidence_items.title: Conversational artificial intelligence for geriatric screening: A mixed-methods feasibility study.

evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into cleft and craniofacial care to facilitate objective assessment, optimize treatment planning, and improve outcome evaluation. By leveraging 3-dimensional imaging, machine learning, and automated workflows, AI addresses key clinical challenges such as anatomic variability, limited robust normative references, and reliance on subjective expertise. Recent developments enable streamlined data acquisition and automated design of surgical devices. This article reviews current applications and highlights clinically relevant advances toward integrated digital workflows and emerging digital twin concepts, with the goal of improving precision, efficiency, and accessibility across cleft and craniofacial treatment pathways.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cleft and Craniofacial Care.

evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence is advancing quickly in orthopaedic imaging, yet remarkably, few tools have entered daily surgical practice. The most convincing near-term use cases for orthopaedic surgeons are tasks that are repetitive, time-consuming, and prone to error; automated landmark detection with subsequent coronal-plane planning for high tibial osteotomy fits that description. Deep learning can localize the anatomical landmarks required for lower-limb alignment analysis and compute a correction angle in seconds, with reproducibility that approaches experienced readers, standardizing measurement and, at scale, letting surgeons iterate across large radiographic datasets and simulate osteotomies for research and training. Two limitations deserve equal attention. One is inherent to planning itself: a coronal, angle-based model cannot represent the 3-dimensional consequences of a posterosuperiorly ascending osteotomy on the axial or sagittal plane nor the intra-articular and ligamentous contributions to deformity. The other is specific to the tool: a system trained on selected, high-quality radiographs should be able to recognize when it should not analyze an image, for example, under insufficient radiographic quality because of malrotation or with retained hardware. Systems may still have a way to go prior to routine use; the distance from a promising prototype to a dependable instrument runs through increasing robustness in clinical reality, independent validation, and an awareness of what 2-dimensional planning cannot capture. Ultimately, the greatest potential will lie in translation from plan to execution, which is where artificial intelligence working with 3-dimensional data may lift osteotomy care to the next level. Until then, the efficiency gains reported in the present study may accelerate planning for high tibial osteotomy by roughly the time it takes to drink a coffee.
evidence_items.title: Editorial Commentary: A Coffee's Worth of Time: Artificial Intelligence May Accelerate, Not Replace, Preoperative Planning for High Tibial Osteotomy.

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Background In the growing field of interventional radiology, emerging technologies implement the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to help tackle growing demands for treatment. Due to the anatomical differences in animals, volunteers offer the most realistic training and testing scenario, however safety considerations restrict rapid prototyping of these new technologies. Simulators have been a key facilitator in the testing of new technologies among numerous medical engineering studies, but often lack the realism to reliably test AI. Purpose This proof‐of‐concept study presents methods to create or enhance hyper‐realistic radiographic simulators that can effectively function with a medical‐grade AI software. Methods Iron‐filled plastic was used to three‐dimensionally (3D) print a series of blocks of heights up to 30 mm. By analyzing the intensities generated by different thicknesses of plastic, anonymous fluoroscopic images were turned into height maps (lithophanes) and 3D‐printed. A static scene from transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) was then 3D‐printed and imaged with different presets using two different x‐ray systems for mathematical analysis. Lithophanes were then used as a radiographic background to experimental and commercial interventional simulators to test Caranx Medical's TAVIPILOT AI. Finally, fluoroscopies from 5 3D‐printed lithophanes were mixed with 5 real images and presented to 5 expert volunteers to establish their realism in a structured survey. Results The 3D‐printed x‐ray lithophanes test‐plates' radiographic appearance was rated as “Adequate” to “Good” across all fields of the survey, with participants praising their realism. The test‐plate was able to reliably recreate the TAVI scene in different x‐ray systems, with joint‐histogram correlation coefficients above 0.9, and global structural similarity above 0.8. The lithophanes were imaged as a standalone test plate and as a backing to dynamic TAVI interventional simulators; in both cases, TAVIPILOT AI responded to the simulator as if it was operating on a real anatomical image. Conclusions Lithophane plates present an easy‐to‐implement solution to recreate monoplane x‐ray scenes, which can be deployed to test software at the point of care with minimal logistical, ethical, or safety concerns. This study opens the door for a new range of interventional simulators able to recreate human‐like appearance to test AI, offering a non‐exclusive alternative to patient volunteers and anonymous data.
evidence_items.title: Development and evaluation of X‐ray lithophanes as test objects for interventional procedure simulation

evidence_items.summary:
This study examines how control allocation between users and artificial intelligence (AI) systems shapes reuse intention in AI-enabled travel planning and whether this effect operates through user experience (UX), cognitive reappraisal, expressive suppression, psychological empowerment and satisfaction.
 
 
 
 Two scenario-based studies were conducted. A laboratory pilot (n = 92) validated system-dominant, shared-control and user-dominant planning conditions. A main online study (n = 463) tested the proposed serial process using confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modeling and 5,000-resample bootstrapping.
 
 
 
 Control allocation significantly affected UX. More favorable UX increased cognitive reappraisal and reduced expressive suppression, and these two regulatory routes had opposite effects on psychological empowerment. Empowerment enhanced satisfaction, which subsequently predicted reuse intention. A supplementary analysis further indicated that AI usage experience conditioned the relationships between UX and emotion regulation.
 
 
 
 AI travel planners should treat control allocation as an interaction-design decision. Modular editing, progressive explanations, reversible changes and adaptive control can preserve user agency while retaining the efficiency benefits of AI assistance.
 
 
 
 This study extends continuance research by identifying the upstream psychological process through which satisfaction is formed under different control-allocation structures. It further distinguishes UX as an evaluative appraisal from emotion regulation as a subsequent coping process in AI-enabled travel planning.
evidence_items.title: How control allocation in AI-enabled travel planning shapes reuse intention: the roles of user experience, emotion regulation and psychological empowerment

evidence_items.summary: Advances in analytical characterisation, functional assays, pharmacokinetic evaluation and manufacturing science have enabled regulatory agencies to increasingly rely on the totality of evidence, reducing the need for comparative clinical efficacy trials in scientifically justified circumstances. Consequently, the principal challenge surrounding biosimilars has shifted from demonstrating biosimilarity to ensuring their effective implementation in routine clinical practice. Despite this strong scientific consensus, variability in clinical uptake persists across healthcare systems, limited by professional uncertainty, patient concerns, organisational barriers and inadequate communication. Clinical pharmacists are uniquely positioned to bridge this gap between regulatory science and clinical implementation. This article discusses concrete strategies through which pharmacists translate regulatory confidence into clinical confidence, including interpretation of comparability evidence for prescribers, structured patient counselling to mitigate the nocebo effect and support shared decision-making, coordination of switching and traceability programmes, multidisciplinary education, and pharmacovigilance and real-world evidence generation. Their contributions across hospital, community and ambulatory care settings are explored, together with their strategic role in Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committees, procurement processes and health policy implementation. Beyond facilitating biosimilar adoption, pharmacists contribute to healthcare sustainability by promoting value-based medicine, resilient procurement strategies, responsible resource allocation and environmentally conscious pharmaceutical practices. Future opportunities, including digital pharmacovigilance, artificial intelligence and personalised implementation strategies, are also discussed. Clinical pharmacists should therefore be regarded not only as medicines experts but also as knowledge translators capable of transforming regulatory guidance into patient-centred clinical practice and sustainable healthcare delivery.
evidence_items.title: The Role of Clinical Pharmacists in Translating Regulatory Acceptance of Biosimilars into Routine Clinical Practice.

evidence_items.summary: This article offers a first consolidated historical account of the institutionalisation of the Integration of Gender in Research and Development (IGiRD). We use IGiRD as an analytical umbrella term for policies, instruments and research practices that integrate sex and gender analysis into the content, design, evaluation and governance of research and development. The article centres on how sex and gender analysis became institutionally anchored as a question of research quality, responsibility and societal relevance, while treating gender representation in research careers as a related but distinct issue. Drawing on an event-based historical reconstruction of 186 policy and institutional events from 1957 to 2024, the article traces how IGiRD developed across four partially overlapping pathways: gender equality and anti-discrimination frameworks, women’s advancement in science and technology, health and medical research, and broader integration of sex and gender analysis across research fields and governance structures. Comparing the EU, US, Canada and South Korea, the analysis shows that IGiRD has not followed a single linear trajectory. The EU pathway is distinctive because gender mainstreaming became layered onto supranational research funding and evaluation structures, while North America demonstrates strong sectoral anchoring in health and biomedical research, and South Korea illustrates rapid formal-legal anchoring with incomplete operational embedding. The article contributes to historical-institutionalist science policy research by conceptualising IGiRD institutionalisation as layered, recursive and politically reversible. Formal anchoring in laws, strategies or funding rules matters, but durable change depends on operational embedding through review expertise, guidance, training, monitoring and feedback mechanisms, and on substantive methodological integration in research practice. This perspective clarifies why IGiRD can be stabilised, narrowed or reactivated under changing political conditions and offers policy implications for strengthening gender-sensitive R&I in emerging fields such as artificial intelligence.
evidence_items.title: From Beijing to Brussels: pathways to the integration of gender in research and development (IGIRD)

evidence_items.summary: Potentially toxic trace elements (PTTEs) contamination is a major global food health burden, with lead exposure causing more than 33 million disability-adjusted life years lost in 2021, mainly from cardiovascular effects. Cadmium in food is strongly linked to kidney dysfunction and reproductive toxicity, while arsenic and zinc also pose serious health risks. Exposure occurs through industrial emissions, contaminated air and water. Despite global studies, local data on these elements in South African fruits and vegetables remain limited. The study aims to determine the levels of arsenic, lead, cadmium, and zinc in fruits and vegetables from Thulamela Municipality and assess potential health risks to consumers and compare the levels of the elements to legal requirements. A cross-sectional design will be adopted. Ten commonly consumed fruits and vegetables will be sampled purposively from three supermarkets in Thulamela and analysed for PTTEs using Inductively Coupled Plasma Spectrometry (ICP-MS) at University of Venda, and assessment of dietary exposure among adult consumers aged 18-65 years through 24-hour recall and Quantified Food Frequency Questionnaire (QFFQ). Differences in PTTEs with metal type and food type as factors will be determined using two-way ANOVA. Dietary data will be coded and analysed using Food Finder 3 software linked to SAFOODS to estimate intake. Health risks associated with intake of the PTTEs will be evaluated in terms of estimated daily intake (EDI), target hazard quotient (THQ), hazard index (HI) and Carcinogenic Risk (CR). Statistical analysis will be done using IBM SPSS version 29, and significance set at p<0.05. Measured elements levels will be compared to national legal limits to estimate daily intake and evaluate health risks. Ethical approval will be obtained and participants rights to consent, privacy, and confidentiality, will be protected. Expected outcomes include contamination levels of PTTEs in selected fruits and vegetables and associated health risk assessment.
evidence_items.title: Assessment of Potentially Toxic Trace Elements in commonly consumed fruits and vegetables from Supermarkets and Associated Health Risks in Thulamela Municipality, South Africa: a study protocol.

evidence_items.summary:
This study examines the factors influencing carbon trading system adoption by extending the traditional technology–organisation–environment (TOE) model into the decentralised technology–organisation–environment–technoethics (DT-OET) model.
 
 
 
 This study used a quantitative research design with a cross-sectional approach and collected data from 384 professionals working in related sectors in Bangladesh. Partial least squares-structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was used to analyse the data along with unobserved heterogeneity analysis and importance-performance map analysis (IPMA).
 
 
 
 The structural model shows that organisational readiness, environmental factors and technoethical factors have significant positive effects on carbon trading adoption. Decentralised technology factors do not have a significant direct effect, but their influence is significantly mediated by trust. Interestingly, trust emerges as a strong direct predictor and also significantly mediates the effects of technoethical, environmental and decentralised technology factors on adoption intention.
 
 
 
 The DT-OET instruments of this paper offer organisations a diagnostic framework to assess their readiness for carbon trading. According to the findings, managers need to prioritise top management support, resource allocation and employee training. Policymakers should design clear regulations and build institutional trust, as environmental factors influence adoption both directly and indirectly through trust. Technology providers need to focus on building trust through system reliability, transparency and user education, as trust mediates the relationship between technological factors and adoption intention.
 
 
 
 This paper expands the TOE model by adding technoethics as a new contextual factor. It moves beyond the view of technology as neutral. This addresses a gap in conventional models that overlook psychological processes in adoption decisions. The findings of this study suggest that benchmarking frameworks need to consider trust as a mediating mechanism.
evidence_items.title: Benchmarking carbon trading adoption in emerging economies through extending the TOE framework

evidence_items.summary: Abstract This study addresses the distribution of wild carrot [Daucus carota (L.) ssp. carota], in the hybrid carrot seed [Daucus carota (L.) ssp. sativus (Hoffm.) Arcang.; hereafter Daucus carota] production region of central Oregon. Field surveys conducted in 2022 and 2023 in collaboration with regional partners provided observational data to train a relative risk model (random forest). Integrating 75 known D. carota occurrences, more than 2,000 known absences, and 1,000 randomly generated background points with data on topography, climate, soil, road proximity, and land cover, the model effectively distinguished potential D. carota establishment sites, achieving a high predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.911) against a background dataset. We identified four model-probability cutoff values (using precision–recall F-measure, varying alpha parameter), yielding five risk categories, from very low to very high risk. The moderate to very high risk categories highlight priority areas for monitoring and management to mitigate the risk of D. carota establishment, a concern especially relevant for local hybrid carrot seed production given the potential for cross-pollination and genetic contamination. The resulting risk maps provide a spatially explicit framework for identifying environmentally suitable habitats and potential invasion corridors, supporting early detection and rapid response efforts. By focusing surveillance and management activities within high-risk areas, stakeholders can improve monitoring efficiency, reduce the likelihood of D. carota establishment and spread, and help maintain the genetic integrity of central Oregon’s hybrid carrot seed production system.
evidence_items.title: Predictive mapping of wild carrot (Daucus carota ssp. carota) in central Oregon

evidence_items.summary: A new series of brominated 1,4-dihydropyridine derivatives bearing various aryl and heteroaryl substituents was successfully synthesized through a microwave-assisted multicomponent Hantzsch reaction followed by bromination under solar irradiation. The synthesized compounds were characterized by IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR spectroscopy and elemental analyses. Their insecticidal activities were evaluated against adult and nymphal stages of the cotton aphid, Aphis gossypii, using the leaf-dipping bioassay technique. Biological evaluation demonstrated that all synthesized derivatives exhibited significant insecticidal activity, with nymphs showing greater susceptibility than adults. Among the tested compounds, derivative 5e displayed the highest activity, with LC50 values of 0.18 and 3.03 mg L−1 against nymphs and adults, respectively. To investigate the potential mode of action, molecular docking studies were performed against acetylcholinesterase (AChE). All compounds showed favorable binding affinities toward the enzyme, ranging from −8.3 to −9.0 kcal mol−1. Compound 5d exhibited the strongest predicted binding affinity (−9.0 kcal mol−1), while the biologically most active derivative, 5e, showed a docking score of −8.7 kcal mol−1. The combined biological and computational results indicate that brominated 1,4-dihydropyridine derivatives represent promising lead structures for the development of new insecticidal agents against A. gossypii.
evidence_items.title: Brominated 1,4-dihydropyridine derivatives as potential insecticides against the cotton aphid (Aphis gossypii): synthesis, characterization, biological evaluation, and molecular docking studies

evidence_items.summary: Cancer remains a major global health challenge and one of the leading causes of mortality worldwide. In the present study, a new series of fused nitrogen-containing heterocyclic derivatives was synthesized from a pyridine-based pyrimidinethione key synthon. Hydrazinolysis followed by cyclo-condensation and condensation reactions afforded structurally diverse pyrimidotriazine, triazolopyrimidine, hydrazone, and pyrazolopyrazole derivatives. The antiproliferative activities of the synthesized compounds were evaluated against human lung carcinoma (A549) and human prostate carcinoma (PC3) cell lines, with WI-38 normal human lung fibroblasts used to assess selectivity. Compounds 6 and 8 emerged as the most promising cell-based candidates, displaying the highest activities against A549 and PC3 cells, respectively, together with favorable selectivity toward cancer cells relative to WI-38 normal cells. To investigate a possible mechanism underlying the observed antiproliferative effects, the most active derivatives (6–8) were screened for EGFR kinase inhibition. Compound 7 exhibited the strongest inhibitory activity, surpassing sorafenib and revealing a clear structure–activity relationship within the series. To gain structural insight into target recognition, molecular docking studies were conducted against EGFR (PDB ID: 1M17) and cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2; PDB ID: 2A4L). The docking protocol was validated by re-docking of the corresponding co-crystallized ligands, demonstrating satisfactory reproduction of the experimental binding modes. Compounds 6–8 adopted favorable binding orientations within the ATP-binding pockets of both enzymes. Compound 7 displayed the most favorable EGFR binding profile, whereas compound 6 showed the strongest predicted affinity toward CDK2. The observed interactions emphasized the importance of molecular planarity, aromaticity, hydrogen-bonding capability, and hydrophobic contacts in stabilizing ligand–enzyme complexes. In silico ADME analysis revealed generally acceptable drug-likeness and pharmacokinetic characteristics, with compound-dependent variations in lipophilicity, gastrointestinal absorption, blood–brain barrier permeability, and P-glycoprotein recognition. Collectively, these findings identify compounds 6–8 as promising anticancer candidates, with compounds 6 and 8 representing potent and selective cell-based leads and compound 7 emerging as a promising EGFR-directed scaffold for further optimization. Furthermore, this work expands the chemical space of fused nitrogen heterocycles and provides a useful platform for the development of kinase-targeted anticancer agents.
evidence_items.title: Synthesis, antitumor evaluation, and in silico investigation of pyridine-based pyrimidotriazine and triazolopyrimidine derivatives as potential EGFR-targeted anticancer agents

evidence_items.summary: Two new series of coumarin–thiazole hybrids (6a–i and 9a–h) were designed and synthesized as EGFR/VEGFR-2 dual inhibitors. Hybrids 6a–i demonstrated remarkable antiproliferative activities on different NCI-60 cell lines in a single-dose assay. The antiproliferative activities of the newly synthesized hybrids were evaluated against a panel of three human cancer cell lines (HepG2, HCT-116, and MCF-7). Compounds 6a, 6h, 9a, and 9d were the four most active hybrids. Herein, compound 6a was the most active antiproliferative agent among the 6a–i hybrids, with IC50 values ranging from 2.85 µM to 7.66 µM. At the same time, compound 9d was the most active antiproliferative agent among the 9a–h hybrids, with IC50 values ranging from 3.79 µM to 9.80 µM. Furthermore, hybrids 6a, 6h, 9a, and 9d expressed low cytotoxicity for the normal fetal lung WI-38 cells. Consistent with the mechanistic study, the most potent compounds (6a, 6h, and 9d) displayed remarkable inhibitory effectiveness against EGFR and VEGFR-2. Moreover, the most potent hybrid (6a) caused the upregulation of Bax, cytochrome c, and caspase-3 levels and downregulation of Bcl-2 levels. Molecular docking study for compounds 6a, 6h, 9a, and 9d agreed with the mechanistic results. Molecular docking into the ATP-binding site of EGFR (PDB: 1M17 and re-docking RMSD = 1.43 Å) and VEGFR-2 (PDB: 4ASD and re-docking RMSD = 1.67 Å) confirmed strong binding affinities for 6a (ΔG = −10.32 and −9.98 kcal mol−1, respectively) and 9d (ΔG = −10.23 and −9.87 kcal mol−1, respectively), consistent with their enzymatic inhibition profiles. To validate the dynamic stability of binding, 100 ns all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were performed for 6a and 9d in complex with EGFR, alongside erlotinib and the apo receptor. Compound 6a was carried forward into the 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations of five systems, comprising the apo receptor, the erlotinib complex and the complexes of 6a, 9d, and 9a. Ligand binding compacted the kinase by roughly 2.3 Å in the radius of gyration relative to the apo receptor and reduced Cα fluctuation across the fold. The total protein–ligand interaction energy ranked the four ligands in an order consistent with the enzymatic assay, yielding values of −69.6, −55.6, −50.6 and −41.7 kcal mol−1 for erlotinib, 6a, 9d and 9a against IC50 values of 0.14, 0.27, 0.378, and 2.94 µM, respectively. Furthermore, every pairwise separation exceeded twice the block-averaged standard error. Compound 6a was identified as the lead compound of the series.
evidence_items.title: New thiazole/coumarin hybrids as EGFR inhibitors with potential VEGFR-2 inhibition (design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and dynamic stimulation)

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
Cross-contamination control is essential in pharmaceutical manufacturing for highly potent and cytotoxic active pharmaceutical ingredients used in oncology products. Epirubicin, an anthracycline antineoplastic agent, requires reliable residue monitoring after cleaning because residual carryover on shared manufacturing equipment may pose quality and safety risks.


OBJECTIVE
This study aimed to develop a practical HPLC-UV-Vis method for epirubicin determination, evaluate its chromatographic performance using solution-based standards and quality-control samples, and apply the method to swab samples collected from contaminated stainless-steel surfaces following different cleaning procedures.


METHODS
Chromatographic separation was achieved on a Poroshell 120 SB-C8 column using an isocratic mobile phase of acetonitrile and purified water containing 0.1% orthophosphoric acid (28:72, v/v) at 0.5 mL/min, with UV-Vis detection at 480 nm, within the visible region. Chromatographic performance was evaluated using solution-based standards and quality-control samples for selectivity, carryover, linearity, sensitivity, accuracy, precision, stability, and system suitability. AISI 304 matte stainless-steel plates were contaminated with epirubicin solution, subjected to different cleaning procedures, and sampled by swabbing. Surface recovery was assessed separately at a single spiking level.


RESULTS
The method was linear over 20-1000 ng/mL. The LOQ was established at 20 ng/mL (S/N = 10.2). The single-level surface-recovery assessment yielded a recovery of 70.5%. Cleaning procedures including 2% sodium hydroxide resulted in no quantifiable parent epirubicin peak under the applied chromatographic conditions.


CONCLUSION
The developed HPLC-UV-Vis method showed suitable chromatographic performance for epirubicin determination under the investigated solution-based conditions and was applied to residue monitoring in swab samples collected from stainless-steel surfaces following cleaning. Because surface recovery was assessed at only one spiking level, the complete surface-sampling and extraction procedure was not comprehensively validated.


HIGHLIGHTS
The developed HPLC-UV-Vis method was applied to epirubicin residue monitoring in swab samples collected from stainless-steel surfaces, with no quantifiable parent epirubicin peak observed after sodium hydroxide-containing cleaning procedures.
evidence_items.title: Development of an HPLC-UV-Vis Method for the Determination of Epirubicin Residues on Stainless-Steel Surfaces.

evidence_items.summary: The critical need to find solutions to antibiotic resistance in pathogenic bacteria is becoming increasingly pronounced globally. In response to the urgent problems posed by the current public health challenges, our study adds to the growing body of knowledge by extracting insect peptides using acidified solvents, identifying the peptides from immune‐challenged and nonimmune‐challenged Schistocerca gregaria nymphs, and evaluating their antimicrobial activities against 9 clinical pathogens. A total of 96 unique peptides were identified, 91% from immune‐challenged nymphs. Three specific antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) were common in immune‐challenged and nonimmune‐challenged individuals. Eleven and 27 peptides were categorized as high‐ and moderate‐confidence AMPs, respectively, with sequence homologies ranging between 33% and 67%. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of peptide extract from immune‐challenged nymphs ranged between 5 and 25 μg/mL, compared to 7.9–100 μg/mL from nonimmune‐challenged nymphs. The lowest MIC values (< 8 μg/mL) were observed against Staphylococcus aureus, Enterococcus faecalis, Listeria monocytogenes, Escherichia coli, and Streptococcus agalactiae. It was observed that 87.5% of the AMP extracts had lower MIC values against Strep. agalactiae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa compared to tetracycline. The hemolytic activities due to peptide extracts from nonimmune‐challenged (SPE‐A) and immune‐challenged (SPE‐B) locust nymphs were < 5%. Our work underscores insects’ promise as sustainable AMP contributors, offering recommendations for further research to unlock their full potential in the design of new antimicrobial agents to overcome bacterial drug resistance.
evidence_items.title: In Silico Characterization of Desert Locust–Derived Antimicrobial Peptides Against Drug‐Resistant Bacteria

evidence_items.summary: A new series of fused thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidine derivatives was designed, synthesized, and comprehensively characterized with the aim of discovering potent insecticidal and antimicrobial agents. The synthetic strategy commenced with the regioselective S-alkylation of ethyl 4-(4-methoxyphenyl)-6-methyl-2-thioxo-1,2,3,4-tetrahydropyrimidine-5-carboxylate (1) with bromomalononitrile to afford the key o-aminothiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidine carbonitrile (2), which was subsequently elaborated via sequential condensation with triethyl orthoformate and hydrazine hydrate into the tricyclic amino–imino pyrimido[4′,5′:4,5]thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidine (4). Divergent cyclocondensation of 4 with triethyl orthoformate, acetylacetone, or benzaldehyde furnished the tetracyclic [1,2,4]triazolo-fused analogues (5–7). All newly synthesized compounds were unequivocally characterized by elemental analysis, FT-IR, 1H and 13C NMR spectroscopy, and mass spectrometry. The antimicrobial activity of the synthesized compounds was evaluated against an array of bacterial and fungal strains using the agar disc diffusion method, while their insecticidal efficacy was assessed against fourth-instar larvae of the cotton leafworm Spodoptera littoralis under laboratory conditions. Compound 4 exhibited the broadest antimicrobial spectrum, whereas compound 5 produced the largest inhibition zone (20.33 mm) against Fusarium oxysporum. In the insecticidal bioassay, compound 7 was the most potent, with an LC50 of 2727.042 mg L−1. Molecular docking studies against acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (CYP450) identified compound 7 as the top-ranked binder for both targets (binding energies of −8.6 and −8.2 kcal mol−1, respectively), establishing a robust structure–activity relationship consistent with the biological data. These findings position the synthesized thiazolo/triazolo-pyrimidine scaffolds as promising lead structures for the development of next-generation insecticidal and antimicrobial agents.
evidence_items.title: Design, synthesis, bioassay, and molecular docking of novel thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidine derivatives as insecticidal and antimicrobial agents

evidence_items.summary: Human cognition flexibly draws on a shared perceptual foundation to understand environments, attend to referenced entities, reason about spatial relationships, and act. Endowing aerial robots with an analogous functional organization remains challenging, as existing systems are often specialized for individual capabilities, dependent on offboard computation, or unable to sustain closed-loop operation on resource-constrained platforms. We present OpenFlyV2, a unified onboard vision-language-action architecture that uses a shared vision-language representation to support semantic understanding, language-grounded perception, spatial reasoning, and continuous aerial control within a single model. A compact action expert converts the shared multimodal context into short-horizon flight waypoints, while motion-aware temporal memory and action priors reduce the computational cost of closed-loop execution. We construct , a simulation-based dataset comprising approximately 70,000 navigation trajectories and 60,000 vision-language instruction--response pairs. OpenFlyV2 generates action chunks, each comprising 12 waypoints, entirely onboard at 10 Hz using an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX. It transfers zero-shot from simulation to physical quadrotor flight, achieving a 48\% navigation success rate across four real-world environments without real-world aerial training data. Extensive results demonstrate that broad vision-language competence and continuous closed-loop flight can coexist within a single model on a resource-constrained aerial platform. Code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/Ideal-ljl/AeroBrain.
evidence_items.title: OpenFlyV2: An onboard vision-language-action model for aerial perception and navigation

evidence_items.summary: We present PhysInsert, a framework for physically plausible reference-based object insertion that jointly adapts objects and their surrounding scenes. Existing methods often rely on masked inputs, generation-based pairs, or training pairs with limited viewpoint variation, leaving pose and illumination adaptation and bidirectional object-scene interactions insufficiently constrained. We construct the Insert World dataset with strictly aligned Blender-rendered counterfactual pairs and object references across viewpoints and lighting conditions. Building on these data, Geometry-Guided Adaptation couples a VGGT geometry stream with image and text streams under target-scene feature supervision to guide spatially consistent insertion. Complementary 2D Object-Scene Spatial Supervision jointly supervises object occupancy and environmental changes while grounding spatial instructions in object regions through image-text attention. We introduce PhysInsert-Bench with dedicated cross-environment and cross-view cases requiring illumination and pose adaptation beyond appearance copying. Experiments on PhysInsert-Bench and DreamBooth demonstrate improved image fidelity; a user study further shows more accurate placement and improved lighting integration, perspective, and pose plausibility.
evidence_items.title: PhysInsert: Physically Plausible Object Insertion with Geometric Priors and Bidirectional Object-Scene Interactions

evidence_items.summary: The hair of stylized characters in games and avatars is built from hair cards: artist-placed ribbons whose geometry is the visible hair, animated by spring bones. Existing image-based methods produce realistic hair or a single fused mesh, while CHARM, the only generator of stylized hair cards, decodes a hairstyle autoregressively as a long sequence of control points. Observing that a card hairstyle is an unordered set of artist-defined primitives, we propose HairDeck, which generates it as one: each card is a single token, and a set diffusion transformer denoises all cards together. From a single image, HairDeck generates the cards and the spring-bone chains that drive them, yielding an animatable asset that exports to ready-to-use downstream formats. On CHARM's own test set, it lowers Chamfer distance by 44% and card-orientation error by more than half while running 33 times faster, and from single images it outperforms CHARM, image-to-3D pipelines and strand-based methods. Project page: https://hyzcluster.github.io/HairDeck
evidence_items.title: HairDeck: Animation-Ready Stylized Hair Cards from a Single Image

evidence_items.summary: One-step and few-step text-to-image generation must accurately render the details specified in the prompt despite limited opportunities for refinement. Distribution matching distillation (DMD) uses score differences to bring the generated distribution closer to a reference distribution. Following prior work, we estimate this difference with internal velocity branches, avoiding a separate fake-score network. We ask whether an explicit moment constraint improves this learned score supervision. A decomposition of the reverse-KL field into a Gaussian moment component and a non-Gaussian residual identifies statistics that can be constrained explicitly. We introduce Intrinsic Distribution Matching (IDM), which retains the full DMD correction and matches feature means and per-coordinate standard deviations using the generator's exponential-moving-average (EMA) copy, requiring no external feature encoder. Experiments use full-parameter and low-rank adaptation (LoRA) tuning on Z-Image-Turbo 6B and Qwen-Image 20B. At two network evaluations, IDM reaches 94.25% and 90.20% on Chinese and English LongText-Bench, the highest scores among the compared methods at this budget. Controlled ablations show gains from the added moment loss, while generator EMA features perform competitively with an external DINOv2 encoder across the five reported metrics. Code is available at https://github.com/inclusionAI/IDM.
evidence_items.title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching

evidence_items.summary: Agentic image editors decompose complex requests into steps, but when a step fails, they mostly retry with the same narrow set of tools and a judge that scores each output by eye directly. We argue that such agents are bounded by two spaces: the action space of what the agent can do, and the observation space of what its judge can see. On our expert-annotated benchmark, a general-purpose editor yields no usable result in over 40% of the cases, and no judge is reliable across edit types. We present EditAgent, which expands both spaces. It routes each step to general editors and specialized methods, and attaches to each candidate a verification record. With these records, off-the-shelf VLM judges outperform finetuned reward models. Candidates are generated in parallel and judged in one listwise call: experts prefer this to sequential refinement in 78.5% of decided comparisons, at no more than half the judge calls. EditAgent improves two open-weight editors on three benchmarks and serves as a data engine for training stronger editors.
evidence_items.title: EditAgent: Rethinking Agentic Image Editing

evidence_items.summary: AI agents no longer act alone: they cooperate, coordinate and compete within and between groups, increasingly alongside humans who are in, on or out of the loop''. Whether such mixed groups can govern themselves is an open question about machine behaviour and human-computer interaction that needs a testbed for hybrid institutions. We present Megabike, a multi-agent simulator and serious game with interdependent arenas for common-pool resource management, cooperative survival and constitutional choice. Riders sharing a megabike must agree their arrangements for steering, pedalling and distributing resources, and their political regime, while negotiating with rival bikes and avoiding an existential threat. Every rule is enforced by the simulator, every action is logged, and any seat can be taken by a human or a machine, so governance can be studied under well-defined metrics. We demonstrate Megabike with forty sessions in which language-model riders with cooperative, lazy, subversive or opposing dispositions chose regimes, elected leaders and expelled one another. The results show that different combinations of agent archetypes could produce unexpected and counterproductive outcomes. We conclude with extensions for systematic experiments mixing human and computational agents.
evidence_items.title: A Simulation Testbed for Self-Governing Human-Machine Institutions

evidence_items.summary: Recent advances in multimodal large language models have increased interest in interaction paradigms for video understanding. The evolution from offline to streaming and proactive interaction has gradually shifted models from passive responders toward more proactive agents that can decide when to answer. However, existing proactive paradigms typically assume that the information required to answer a query is complete, leaving models to only wait or answer. In the real world, however, information is often incomplete due to uncertainty from either the video or the user. In proactive paradigms, such uncertainty can cause the model to wait forever or generate highly hallucinatory responses. We therefore argue that proactive interaction should be redefined with a third action: ask, allowing models to actively ask for missing information. To study when and what models should ask before answering, we introduce AskStream, the first multi-turn benchmark spanning video and user uncertainty for streaming video understanding, with four task categories and eight subtasks. It contains 438 videos with 2,714 manually annotated frame-level time windows across three types: wait, ask, and answer. Across both multiple-choice and open-ended settings, even the strongest model attains only 52.18% on our proposed Ask-F1 metric, highlighting substantial limitations in proactive information seeking under uncertainty.
evidence_items.title: AskStream: When and What to Ask Proactively under Uncertainty in Streaming Video Understanding

evidence_items.summary: Diffusion vision-language models (DVLMs) process their entire input at every denoising step. Since visual tokens make up 89-97% of this input on the benchmarks we study, most of the decoding computation is spent repeatedly processing the same image. Visual token pruning methods partially relieve this burden by removing part of the visual tokens, but they lose the removed information and still process the remaining image at every step. To measure how often the image is actually needed, we compare LLaDA-V's predictions with and without the image at every decoding step and find that removing the image changes a token being unmasked at only 22.8% of steps on average and at as few as 7.9%. We therefore propose LOWN, a decoding method that decides at every step whether to process the image and how many tokens to unmask. LOWN predicts the masked tokens without the image and processes the image only when this prediction disagrees with the last image-conditioned prediction. Agreement certifies the earlier prediction for reuse, and the number of certified tokens sets how many are unmasked in that step. We further observe that the need for the image differs across benchmarks, so LOWN's adaptive decision is needed rather than a fixed schedule. Without training or a tuned threshold, LOWN retains 99.6% of LLaDA-V's score on ten benchmarks at 35.3% of the decoding FLOPs on average. LOWN also generalizes across LLaDA-based DVLMs, composes orthogonally with visual token pruning, and runs under key-value caching for further efficiency gains. Code and project page are available at https://hyeon9698.github.io/LOWN/
evidence_items.title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs

evidence_items.summary: Scaling supervised training for working agents requires diverse professional tasks that yield reliable expert demonstrations. However, missing or inconsistent task information can obstruct teacher execution and weaken the resulting supervision. We propose WorkFactory, a scalable framework for constructing coherent and executable professional tasks. Starting from professional intents, information-level planning builds an information support graph to guide task instantiation, explicitly representing the dependencies and locations of information required for the intended outputs. Probe executions then identify support failures and guide repairs while preserving the intended work. We construct 112,686 tasks spanning 612 occupations and use the collected teacher trajectories to fine-tune Qwen models at 4B, 27B, and 35B-A3B scales, yielding the WorkPilot family. All three models improve over their respective base models across four professional-work benchmarks, with WorkPilot-35B-A3B improving from 879 to 1565 Elo on GDPval-AA v2.1. Scaling analyses reveal model-dependent diminishing returns, with execution length first increasing and then decreasing. Controlled component analyses show that planning and repair reduce probe-diagnosed task environment defects and improve downstream performance. The data and models are available at https://github.com/IQuestLab/WorkFactory.
evidence_items.title: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training

evidence_items.summary: Agentic services alternate between model inference on clustered GPUs and external tools on distributed CPUs. In this scenario, existing systems (1) overlook tool-return readiness in service evaluation, wasting limited resources, and (2) use heuristic strategies to decide admission and placement on GPUs, resulting in suboptimal scheduling decisions. To bridge this gap, we present TAO, a tool-aware joint scheduling framework for LLM-based agentic serving. Its value interface combines near-term tool readiness, node-specific cache credit with time-aware decay, and token footprint; a dynamic program jointly selects and places waiting sessions under capacity constraints. Across the 12 reported model-workload-concurrency settings, TAO reduces latency by up to 26.8%, reduces mean time to first token (TTFT) by up to 36.3%, and increases decode throughput by up to 29.5% relative to the best evaluated state-of-the-art baseline for each metric.
evidence_items.title: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving

evidence_items.summary: Extending Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) to humanoid robots requires coordinated whole-body control and diverse demonstrations that are costly to collect in real-world scenarios. Although egocentric human demonstrations provide a complementary source of task experience, differences in visual embodiment and missing robot proprioception complicate transfer to humanoid policies. To address these challenges, we introduce HuGe, a family of Humanoid Generalist VLAs pre-trained on over 2,000 hours of egocentric human and robot data. Specifically, HuGe employs three existing representative VLA architectures to predict latent motion tokens for a pretrained whole-body controller, together with hand-control signals. Based on this, we introduce a three-stage training pipeline that combines egocentric pre-training, humanoid adaptation, and downstream fine-tuning. To facilitate transfer across embodiments, we construct pseudo-proprioceptive states through simulation playback during pre-training and modify arm appearance in egocentric observations through re-rendering during downstream fine-tuning. With this pipeline, HuGe achieves the state-of-the-art on simulation benchmark HumanoidArena. Furthermore, real-world experiments on the Unitree G1 indicate that augmenting robot demonstrations with visually adapted egocentric demonstrations significantly increases success on a pick-and-drop task.
evidence_items.title: HuGe: Scaling Humanoid Generalist Vision-Language-Action Models with Egocentric Experience

evidence_items.summary: GUI grounding requires locating small controls in cluttered screenshots and identifying which control a natural-language instruction refers to. Cropping and enlargement can expose local detail, but the resulting image may still leave ambiguity about the intended target. We propose PreView, an auxiliary preprocessor that improves the inputs to an existing grounding model without further training that model. PreView prepares two complementary types of input features: task-relevant views for localization and candidate-specific cues for target understanding. A trained lightweight auxiliary model predicts and refines a center, crops the screenshot into a local view, and enlarges that view for zoomed-in grounding. It also prepares a visual cue (i.e., a red-circle marker with a location hint) and a textual cue describing the candidate's identity or function. The frozen grounding model uses the prepared inputs to predict the final click. Across five benchmarks, PreView improves the average grounding accuracy of Qwen3-VL-2B, OS-Atlas-4B, and Qwen3-VL-4B without further training these grounding models. Extensive analyses examine the contributions of views and cues, center refinement, and visual input budgets.
evidence_items.title: PreView: Enhancing GUI Grounding with Preprocessed Views and Cues

evidence_items.summary: Standard sequence models encode position by token rank rather than physical coordinate, typically forcing practitioners to destructively resample continuous physical signals such as spectra observed across heterogeneous instruments. We identify this coordinate mismatch as a structural limitation in cross-instrument representation learning, and propose OmniSpectra, a wavelength-native foundation model for spectral representation learning: a continuous-coordinate masked autoencoder that discards the integer pixel indexing of sequence modeling. Mapping physical coordinates to a logarithmic basis turns the multiplicative scaling induced by cosmological redshift into a uniform additive shift. In continuous rotary position embeddings, this shared shift cancels from relative token distances rather than producing grid-dependent positional distortion. We further counter the spectral bias inherent to implicit neural decoders with a physics-grounded, resolution-gated Fourier decoder that provides anti-aliasing. Pretrained on eight surveys and benchmarked against seven baselines, our model reaches state-of-the-art performance with only 12.2M parameters while outperforming substantially larger models, indicating that encoding physical structure can substitute for parameter scale.
evidence_items.title: OmniSpectra: A Unified Foundation Model for Universal Spectra Representation Learning

evidence_items.summary: Robot foundation models are typically evaluated through costly closed-loop rollouts, motivating low-cost offline proxies for model capability. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that as representations improve, modalities such as vision and language converge toward a shared statistical model of reality. We ask whether motion trajectories form another such modality: as embodied models become more capable, should their sensory representations converge toward the structure of physical motion? To test this, we propose Sensorimotor Alignment (S^2), a training-free offline metric that measures how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion. We find that S^2 correlates positively with downstream robot task success across model families, making it a low-cost offline proxy for prioritizing models before closed-loop evaluation. S^2 can also identify promising vision-language model (VLM) backbones before costly fine-tuning into vision-language-action models (VLAs). Beyond this correlation, S^2 offers representation-level explanations for phenomena observed in VLAs and world action models (WAMs). With S^2, we extend PRH to robotics and make sensorimotor alignment measurable, offering a low-cost, representation-level view of robot foundation models that closed-loop success rates alone cannot reveal.
evidence_items.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success

evidence_items.summary: Spoken Dialogue Models (SDMs) typically share a speech-token space for generation and synthesis, leading to long autoregressive sequences and costly inference. Lower-rate speech tokenizers shorten sequences but may introduce compression-quality trade-offs and costly replacement without breaking this coupling. To address this limitation, we propose CoSTA, a compatibility-preserving post-hoc framework that decouples generation and synthesis token spaces while retaining the original speech tokenizer and decoder. CoSTA extends the generation token space with compressed representations via mean-initialized vocabulary extension, pronunciation adaptation, and dialogue adaptation, followed by deterministic expansion back to the original speech-token space before synthesis. On bilingual speech-dialogue benchmarks, CoSTA achieves approximately 1.7times expanded speech-token generation speed, lower full-response latency, and higher throughput while preserving response quality. Analyses show more sustained interaction under limited budgets and a practical trade-off among compression, decoding efficiency, and quality. Further experiments demonstrate cross-architecture transfer and complementarity to low-rate tokenization.
evidence_items.title: CoSTA: Compressed Speech Token Adaptation for Efficient Spoken Dialogue Models

evidence_items.summary: Despite their extensive pretraining knowledge and strong reasoning capabilities, large language models (LLMs) struggle to adaptively gather information in experimental design tasks. We study how to amortize sequential Bayesian experimental design (BED) into an LLM by explicitly training the reasoning that guides action selection using information-gain rewards. Our approach specifies the experimental generative model independently of the LLM's own beliefs, allowing us to optimize expected information gain under a model of our choosing. We investigate the design choices for amortization, including alternative generative-model constructions, reward estimation, hypothesis-space specification, multi-step objectives, and computational costs relative to training- and inference-time BED baselines. On Twenty Questions, the resulting policies improve information acquisition and task performance, outperform inference- and training-time BED baselines at substantially lower computational cost, and generalize to unseen categories. We further demonstrate positive transfer from Twenty Questions training to Medi-Q, a real-world clinical dialogue benchmark. These results suggest that information gathering can be learned as a generalizable reasoning skill in LLMs.
evidence_items.title: Amortizing Sequential Experimental Design in Reasoning LLMs

answers.question: What should someone building or evaluating AI systems do differently today?
answers.signal: In this captured feed, releases and updates dominate, while benchmark and evaluation tags are common. New artifacts emphasize specification quality, test coverage, leakage auditing, executable checks, and verifying whether an agent’s report matches its recorded actions and state.
answers.signal_zh: 在本次采集的信息流中，发布和更新占主导地位，而基准与评估标签也很常见。新产物强调规范质量、测试覆盖、泄漏审计、可执行检查，以及验证智能体的报告是否与其记录的操作和状态一致。
answers.takeaway: Add a benchmark-adoption gate covering task fit, data provenance, leakage, test coverage, reproducible setup, version pinning, and action logging. Evaluate against your own likely failures alongside public suites, and distinguish a new release from an update or an attention signal.
answers.takeaway_zh: 建立基准采用门槛，涵盖任务适配性、数据来源、泄漏、测试覆盖、可复现设置、版本锁定和操作日志记录。在使用公开套件的同时，也应针对自身可能出现的故障进行评估，并区分新发布、更新和关注度信号。

answers.counter_view: Because the observation windows are certified comparable and the category measures span many sources and persistent histories, the lower recent averages could indicate a genuine slowdown in this captured feed. That competing reading remains limited to radar activity and does not demonstrate reduced research output, quality, or adoption across the field.
answers.counter_view_zh: 由于观察窗口经确认具有可比性，且类别指标覆盖众多来源和持续积累的历史记录，近期平均值下降可能表明本次采集的信息流确实放缓。这种不同解读仍仅限于雷达活动，无法证明整个领域的研究产出、质量或采用程度有所下降。
answers.plain_chinese: 数量仅反映该雷达采集到了什么，并不能说明系统是否变得更好或更安全。缺失的证据包括独立复测、相同设置下的直接比较、生产环境结果、污染检查，以及对下载量变化反映真实使用而非托管或采集效应的确认。
answers.plain_english: Counts show what this radar captured, not whether systems became better or safer. Missing evidence includes independent reruns, direct comparisons under the same setup, production outcomes, contamination checks, and confirmation that download changes reflect real use rather than hosting or collection effects.
answers.question: What does today's evidence fail to show, and what would change the reading?
answers.signal: The feed does not establish broad field direction, benchmark quality, production impact, or adoption. Recent daily averages are lower across the tracked categories, but that is a feed-level observation. Multi-source sightings are uncommon, and reported download movements cover differing full tracked spans without corroboration.
answers.signal_zh: 该信息流无法证明整个领域的发展方向、基准质量、生产影响或采用情况。近期日均值在各追踪类别中都较低，但这只是信息流层面的观察。多来源发现并不常见，而且所报告的下载量变动覆盖不同的完整追踪区间，也没有得到佐证。
answers.takeaway: The reading would change with repeated independent evaluations using pinned versions and shared protocols, broader source coverage, production-relevant outcome measurements, and movement confirmed by multiple data sources. Until then, interpret lower recent activity and cumulative download changes as monitoring signals rather than field conclusions.
answers.takeaway_zh: 如果有使用锁定版本和统一协议的重复独立评估、更广泛的来源覆盖、与生产相关的结果测量，以及经多个数据源确认的变动，当前解读就会改变。在此之前，应将近期活动减少和累计下载量变化视为监测信号，而非对整个领域的结论。
